# Ella SMSC Documentation

> An SMS Service Center for private 4G and 5G networks - easy to operate, reliable, and secure.

An SMS Service Center for private 4G and 5G networks - easy to operate, reliable, and secure.

# Home

# Ella SMSC

**Ella SMSC** lets private cellular network subscribers send and receive SMS messages. It is an SMS Service Center (SMSC) that integrates with 4G and 5G core networks.

## Key features

- **SMS over NAS**: phones on 4G and 5G send and receive SMS through the MME or SMSF of the core over SGd.
- **SMS over IP**: phones registered with an IP-SM-GW, such as Ella IMS's, send and receive SMS through it.
- **Store and forward**: messages wait while a phone is unreachable, are retried, and go out as soon as the HSS says it is back, within their validity period.
- **Application messages**: send messages to phones from the web UI, the HTTP API, or SMPP 3.4 for SIM OTA platforms and other ESMEs.
- **Delivery visibility**: every routing lookup and delivery attempt is recorded, with why it failed.
- **Single sign-on**: users log in with your identity provider, such as Google, Microsoft or Okta, over OpenID Connect.
- **Secure**: users with roles, API tokens, HTTPS, and audited reads of message content.
- **Scalable**: serve SMS to up to 100,000 subscribers.
- **Highly available**: deploy Ella SMSC as a high-availability cluster to ensure continuous operation with failover capabilities.
- **Easy to operate**: a single binary with an embedded database and configurable retention, a web UI, an HTTP API, and Prometheus metrics. Install with snap, Docker or Kubernetes.

# Tutorials

# Tutorials

In this tutorial, we will add SMS to a private 5G network with Ella SMSC.

| Tutorial                                                                               | Hardware Required                   | Installation Method | Duration |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------- |
| [Send Your First SMS](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/tutorials/first_sms/index.md) | An Ella Core 5G network, two phones | Snap                | ~15 min  |

# Send Your First SMS

In this tutorial, we will add Ella SMSC to a private 5G network running Ella Core, and send an SMS between two phones.

You can expect to spend about 15 minutes completing this tutorial.

## Pre-requisites

To complete this tutorial, you will need:

- A 5G network running Ella Core, as built in Ella Core's [Getting Started (5G Network with Radio Hardware)](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/tutorials/getting_started_hardware/) tutorial, with PLMN `00101`.
- Two phones attached to the network, with SIM cards whose SMSC number you can set.

## 1. Install Ella SMSC

On the host running Ella Core, install and start the Ella SMSC snap:

```
sudo snap install ella-smsc
sudo snap start --enable ella-smsc.smscd
```

## 2. Initialize Ella SMSC

Open your browser at `http://<host-ip>:5010`. The **Initialize Ella SMSC** page opens.

Enter an email and a password of at least 8 characters, and click **Create**.

The **Diameter** page shows no connected peers yet.

## 3. Connect Ella Core

In the Ella Core UI, go to **Operator** and scroll to the **SMS** section.

Click **Add Service Center** and set:

- **Address**: `127.0.0.1`
- **Numbers**: `+15550000000`
- **Diameter Identity**: the **Host** of Ella SMSC's **Diameter** page, e.g. `smsc-013c0a7ca824.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`

Click **Add**. The service center shows **Connected**.

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to **Diameter**. Under **Connected Peers**, Ella Core shows **open**, with **HSS** set to **yes**.

## 4. Give the subscribers an MSISDN

In the Ella Core UI, for each of the two subscribers:

- Go to **Subscribers** and open the subscriber.
- In **Provisioning**, click the edit icon next to **MSISDN**.
- Enter `+15551230001` for the first subscriber and `+15551230002` for the second, and click **Update**.

## 5. Set the SMSC number on the SIM cards

On each SIM card, set the SMSC number to `+15550000000`.

## 6. Send an SMS

From the first phone, send `hello` to `+15551230002`. The second phone receives it.

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to **Messages**. The message shows **delivered**. Click it to see its routing and delivery attempts.

You have added SMS to your 5G network.

## Next steps

- [Integrate with Ella IMS](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/integrate_with_ella_ims/index.md) to deliver SMS over IP.
- [Send messages from an application](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/send_messages_from_an_application/index.md).

# Back Up and Restore

A backup holds message content, user accounts, and the single sign-on client secret. Store and transfer it encrypted.

## Back up

1. Create an API token for an admin: in **Users**, open the user, and in **API Tokens**, click **Create Token**.

1. Download a backup:

   ```
   curl -OJ http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/backup \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..."
   ```

   This saves `smsc-backup-<time>.tar.gz`. In a cluster, back up from any node.

## Restore

1. Log in as an admin, and keep the token:

   ```
   TOKEN=$(curl -s http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/auth/login \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"email": "admin@example.com", "password": "..."}' | jq -r .result.token)
   ```

1. Restore the backup:

   ```
   curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/restore \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/gzip" \
     --data-binary @smsc-backup-<time>.tar.gz
   ```

   In a cluster, restore on any node.

## Disaster recovery

Use this procedure when a cluster lost a majority of its nodes, or a standalone node was lost.

1. Install Ella SMSC on a new host, as in [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/install/index.md). For a cluster, add a `cluster` block to the configuration file.

1. Open `http://<host-ip>:5010` in a browser and initialize it with a temporary user.

1. Restore the backup with that user, as in [Restore](#restore).

1. For a standalone deployment, stop here.

1. Log in with a user from the backup, and add the other nodes, as in [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md), steps 2 to 4. Delete the data of any node that was in the old cluster first:

   ```
   sudo snap stop ella-smsc.smscd
   sudo rm -rf /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.db* /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/raft
   sudo snap start ella-smsc.smscd
   ```

# Configure Single Sign-On

This guide lets users sign in to the Ella SMSC UI through an OpenID Connect identity provider. It gives the steps for Keycloak; other providers are set up the same way.

## Prerequisites

- **Ella SMSC**: served over HTTPS, at a URL with no path.
- **Identity provider**: an OpenID Connect provider, reachable from Ella SMSC over HTTPS.
- **Ella SMSC account**: an Admin that signs in with a password.

The examples use these values:

| Value                                                | Role                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `https://smsc.example.com`                           | Ella SMSC's external URL                                                |
| `https://smsc.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback` | Redirect URL: the external URL followed by `/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback` |

## 1. Register Ella SMSC at the identity provider

In the realm users sign in to:

1. Go to **Clients** and click **Create client**.
1. Set **Client type** to **OpenID Connect** and **Client ID** to `smsc`. Click **Next**.
1. Turn on **Client authentication**. Keep **Standard flow** checked. Click **Next**.
1. Set **Valid redirect URIs** to the redirect URL. Click **Save**.
1. In the client's **Credentials** tab, copy the **Client Secret**.

In **Users**, turn on **Email verified** for each user.

1. Register a web application, or confidential client, with the redirect URL.
1. Create a client secret for it.
1. Allow the `openid`, `email` and `profile` scopes.

If the provider does not send `email_verified`, turn on **Trust email addresses from this provider** in step 2.

## 2. Configure Ella SMSC

In the UI, go to **Single Sign-On** and, in **Provider**, click **Edit**. Set:

| Field                                        | Value                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **External URL**                             | `https://smsc.example.com`                                                                  |
| **Issuer URL**                               | Keycloak: `https://<keycloak-host>/realms/<realm>`. Otherwise, from the provider.           |
| **CA certificate**                           | The PEM CA certificate of the identity provider, only if a private CA signs its certificate |
| **Client ID**                                | Keycloak: `smsc`. Otherwise, from the provider.                                             |
| **Client secret**                            | The secret from step 1                                                                      |
| **Display name**                             | The name on the login button, such as `Keycloak`                                            |
| **Scopes**                                   | `openid email profile`                                                                      |
| **Session lifetime**                         | `24` hours, or less to end access sooner after offboarding                                  |
| **Trust email addresses from this provider** | Off, unless the provider does not send `email_verified`                                     |

Check that the **Redirect URL** under the external URL is the one registered in step 1.

## 3. Test the identity provider

In the dialog, click **Test**. Fix the issuer URL or the CA certificate until it shows **Works**. Click **Update**.

## 4. Enable single sign-on

On the **Single Sign-On** page, click **Enable**.

To turn it off, for example during an incident, click **Disable**. Everyone who logged in with single sign-on is signed out.

## 5. Sign in

1. Give a user access: [create their user](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/manage_single_sign_on_users/#give-a-user-access), or [map their groups to a role](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/manage_single_sign_on_users/#map-groups-to-roles).
1. In a private browser window, open `https://smsc.example.com`, and click **Log in with** your display name.
1. Sign in at the identity provider. Ella SMSC opens.

If the login page shows an error, the `auth_oidc_login` [audit event](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/observability/#audit-events) in the logs gives the reason.

# Connect through Diameter Agents

This guide connects Ella SMSC to an edge agent (DEA), to deliver short messages to roaming subscribers, and to a DRA in front of the HSS.

## Prerequisites

- **Ella SMSC**: integrated with its core, as in [Integrate with a Third-Party Core](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/integrate_with_third_party_core/index.md).
- **A user** with the Network Manager or Admin role.
- **The agents**: their Diameter hosts and SCTP addresses. Each has Ella SMSC's host, realm and Diameter address as a peer.
- **The visited networks**: support SMS in MME (SGd), or an SMSF with a Diameter host and realm.

The examples use these values:

| Value                                                 | Role                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `dea1.ipx.example.net`, `192.0.2.10`, `198.51.100.10` | Edge agent              |
| `dra1.example.net`, `10.3.0.20`                       | DRA in front of the HSS |
| `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`                   | Ella SMSC's realm       |

## 1. Add the edge agent

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to **Diameter** and click **Add Peer**:

- **Host**: `dea1.ipx.example.net`
- **Addresses**: `192.0.2.10, 198.51.100.10`, every SCTP address of the agent.
- **Port**: `3868`

Click **Add Route**, and keep **Application** set to **SGd** and **Destination** to **Default**. Click **Add**.

To add a backup agent, repeat with its host and addresses, and set the route's **Priority** to `1`.

When an agent fails with a message in flight, Ella SMSC sends the message through the backup, and the subscriber may receive it twice.

## 2. Add the DRA

Skip this step if the HSS connects to Ella SMSC.

Click **Add Peer**:

- **Host**: `dra1.example.net`
- **Addresses**: `10.3.0.20`
- **Port**: `3868`

Click **Add Route**, and set:

- **Application**: **S6c**
- **Destination**: **Realm**
- **Realm**: `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`

Click **Add**.

## 3. Verify

On the **Diameter** page, under **Configured Peers**:

- Each agent shows **open**. Hover over another state to see why.
- The DRA shows **HSS** set to **yes**.

Send a short message to a roaming subscriber. On the **Messages** page, it shows **delivered**.

# Deploy a High Availability Cluster

Ella SMSC can be deployed as a high-availability cluster to provide redundancy and failover capabilities. See [High Availability](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/explanation/high_availability/index.md) for more information.

## Prerequisites

- Three hosts meeting the standard [system requirements](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/system_reqs/index.md).
- Ella SMSC installed on each host via the [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/install/index.md) guide, with a `cluster` block in the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/config_file/index.md).

## 1. Start node 1

Start node 1, open a browser at the API address and initialize it normally.

## 2. Create a join token for node 2

Still in node 1, open the **Cluster** page, click **Add Node**, click **Create Token**, then copy the token.

## 3. Start node 2

Start node 2, open a browser at the API address and click **Join an existing cluster instead**. Paste the token and click **Join**.

## 4. Add node 3

Repeat steps 2 and 3 for node 3.

## 5. Connect the Diameter peers

Connect every Diameter peer, such as Ella Core, the HSS or Ella IMS, to every node, with each node's address and Diameter host. The **Cluster** page lists each node's **Diameter Host**. Or connect the nodes and the peers through a Diameter routing agent, as in [Connect through Diameter Agents](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/connect_through_diameter_agents/index.md).

## 6. Verify

On the **Cluster** page, all three nodes appear as **Healthy**.

# Install

Choose one of the installation methods below.

Install the Ella SMSC snap:

```
sudo snap install ella-smsc
```

Configure Ella SMSC:

```
sudo vim /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.yaml
```

Start Ella SMSC:

```
sudo snap start --enable ella-smsc.smscd
```

Install the required dependencies:

```
sudo snap install go --channel=1.27/stable --classic
sudo snap install node --channel=24/stable --classic
sudo apt update
sudo apt -y install gcc
```

Clone the Ella SMSC repository:

```
git clone https://github.com/ellanetworks/smsc.git
cd smsc
```

Build the frontend:

```
npm install --prefix ui
npm run build --prefix ui
```

Build Ella SMSC:

```
go build -o smsc -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/ellanetworks/smsc/version.GitCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ./cmd/smsc
```

Configure Ella SMSC:

```
vim smsc.yaml
```

Start Ella SMSC:

```
./smsc --config smsc.yaml
```

Create a new directory:

```
mkdir ella-smsc
cd ella-smsc
```

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml

```
configs:
  ella_smsc_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        level: info
      db:
        path: /data/smsc.db
      api:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port: 5010
      diameter:
        address: 10.3.0.7

services:
  ella-smsc:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-smsc:latest
    configs:
      - source: ella_smsc_config
        target: /smsc.yaml
    entrypoint: /bin/smsc --config /smsc.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    stop_grace_period: 50s
    network_mode: host
    volumes:
      - ella-smsc-data:/data

volumes:
  ella-smsc-data:
```

Set `diameter.address` to an address of the host that the core can reach.

Start the Ella SMSC container:

```
docker compose up -d
```

Ensure your Kubernetes cluster is running with the [Multus CNI](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/multus-cni) installed, and the `sctp` kernel module loaded on its nodes.

Download the Ella SMSC manifests:

```
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/smsc.git
```

Edit `smsc/k8s/smsc-diameter-nad.yaml` to set `master` to the host interface that connects to your core, and set the Diameter address. Use the same address for `diameter.address` in `smsc/k8s/smsc-configmap.yaml`.

Deploy Ella SMSC:

```
kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl apply -k smsc/k8s
```

Ella SMSC's UI and API are on the `ella-smsc` NodePort Service.

Ella SMSC's UI and API are at `http://<host-ip>:5010`. Open the UI and create the first user.

See the [configuration reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/config_file/index.md) for all options.

# Integrate with Ella Core

This guide connects Ella SMSC to Ella Core, with Ella Core as the HSS (S6c) and the MME or SMSF (SGd).

## Prerequisites

- **Ella SMSC**: installed and started, as in [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/install/index.md).

The examples use these values:

| Value          | Role                               |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `10.3.0.7`     | Ella SMSC's Diameter address       |
| `001` / `01`   | Ella Core's MCC and MNC            |
| `+15550000000` | Ella SMSC's service centre address |
| `+15550001111` | Ella Core's SMS number             |

## 1. Set the Diameter address

In `smsc.yaml`, set the address Ella Core reaches Ella SMSC on, and restart Ella SMSC:

```
diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.7
```

## 2. Set the operator

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to the **Operator** page:

- Click the edit icon next to **Operator ID (MCC/MNC)**, enter Ella Core's MCC and MNC, e.g. `001` / `01`, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **Service Centre Address**, enter `+15550000000`, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **Numbering**, enter your country code and prefixes, and click **Update**.

Go to the **Diameter** page and note the **Host**, e.g. `smsc-013c0a7ca824.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`.

## 3. Add Ella SMSC to Ella Core

In the Ella Core UI, go to **Operator** and scroll to the **SMS** section:

- Check that **SMS Number** is set, e.g. `+15550001111`, Ella Core's default.
- Click **Add Service Center**, enter:
  - **Address**: `10.3.0.7`
  - **Numbers**: `+15550000000`
  - **Diameter Identity**: the **Host** of step 2.
- Click **Add**.

The service center shows **Connected**.

## 4. Give subscribers an MSISDN

In the Ella Core UI, for each subscriber that sends or receives SMS, go to **Subscribers**, open the subscriber, click the edit icon next to **MSISDN**, enter its E.164 number, e.g. `+15551230001`, and click **Update**.

## 5. Set the SMSC number on the SIM cards

On each SIM card, set the SMSC number to `+15550000000`.

## 6. Verify

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to **Diameter**. Under **Connected Peers**, Ella Core shows **open**, with **HSS** set to **yes**.

Send an SMS between two phones. On the **Messages** page, it shows **delivered**.

# Integrate with Ella IMS

This guide lets Ella SMSC deliver SMS to phones registered for SMS over IP with Ella IMS's IP-SM-GW. Phones send SMS over IP to Ella SMSC the same way.

## Prerequisites

- **Ella SMSC**: connected to Ella Core, as in [Integrate with Ella Core](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/integrate_with_ella_core/index.md).
- **Ella IMS**: connected to Ella Core, as in Ella IMS's [Integrate with Ella Core](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/integrate_with_ella_core/).

The examples use `10.3.0.7` as Ella SMSC's Diameter address and `+15550000000` as its service centre address.

## 1. Enable SMS over IP in Ella IMS

Follow Ella IMS's [Enable SMS over IP](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/enable_sms_over_ip/) guide. When you add the SMSC, enter:

- **Address**: `10.3.0.7`
- **Roles**: **SGd** only
- **Service Centres**: `15550000000`
- **Transport**: **SCTP**
- **Host**: the **Host** of Ella SMSC's **Diameter** page, e.g. `smsc-013c0a7ca824.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`

## 2. Verify

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to **Diameter**. Under **Connected Peers**, Ella IMS shows **open**, with **Applications** set to **SGd** and **HSS** set to **no**.

Send an SMS to a phone registered for SMS over IP. On the **Messages** page, click the message: its delivery attempt went to Ella IMS's host, marked **(IP-SM-GW)**.

# Integrate with a Third-Party Core

This guide connects Ella SMSC to a 4G or 5G core other than Ella Core, through its HSS (S6c) and its MMEs or SMSFs (SGd).

## Prerequisites

- **Ella SMSC**: installed and started, as in [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/install/index.md).
- **HSS**: supports S6c, in the realm `epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org` of the core's PLMN.
- **MME or SMSF**: supports SGd, and gives the MSISDN of the phone in each short message it forwards. The HSS names it, in its routing answers, by the Diameter identity it connects to Ella SMSC with.

The examples use `10.3.0.7` as Ella SMSC's Diameter address, `001` / `01` as the core's MCC and MNC, and `+15550000000` as Ella SMSC's service centre address.

## 1. Set the Diameter address

In `smsc.yaml`, set the address the core reaches Ella SMSC on, and restart Ella SMSC:

```
diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.7
```

## 2. Set the operator

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to the **Operator** page:

- Click the edit icon next to **Operator ID (MCC/MNC)**, enter the core's MCC and MNC, e.g. `001` / `01`, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **Service Centre Address**, enter `+15550000000`, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **Numbering**, enter your country code and prefixes, and click **Update**.

The **Diameter** page shows Ella SMSC's **Host** and **Realm**, e.g. `smsc-013c0a7ca824.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org` and `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`.

## 3. Add Ella SMSC to the core

In the HSS, and in each MME or SMSF, add Ella SMSC as a Diameter peer:

- **Address**: `10.3.0.7`
- **Port**: `3868`
- **Transport**: SCTP
- **Host** and **Realm**: those of step 2.
- **Application**: S6c in the HSS, SGd in the MME or SMSF.

In each MME or SMSF, route the short messages of service centre address `+15550000000` to Ella SMSC.

## 4. Provision the subscribers

In the HSS, give each subscriber that sends or receives SMS an MSISDN. On each SIM card, set the SMSC number to `+15550000000`.

## 5. Verify

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to **Diameter**. Under **Connected Peers**:

- The HSS shows **open**, with **HSS** set to **yes**. If it shows **no**, its realm differs from Ella SMSC's, or it does not support S6c.
- Each MME or SMSF shows **open**, with **SGd** in **Applications**.

Send an SMS between two phones. On the **Messages** page, it shows **delivered**.

See [Connectivity](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/connectivity/index.md) and [3GPP Compliance](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/3gpp_compliance/index.md) for the interfaces Ella SMSC supports.

# Manage Single Sign-On Users

These guides manage users who sign in through the identity provider. [Configure single sign-on](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/configure_single_sign_on/index.md) first.

## Give a user access

1. In the UI, go to **Users** and click **Create**. Set:
   - **Email**: the user's email address at the identity provider
   - **Password**: off
   - **Role**: the user's role
   - **Pin role**: checked to keep this role, if groups are mapped to roles
1. Click **Create**.

The user signs in with **Log in with** the display name. Their first login links their user to their account at the identity provider.

## Map groups to roles

Users in a mapped group get their role from it at each login, and get a user at their first login. Users in no mapped group cannot sign in through the identity provider, unless their role is [pinned](#pin-a-users-role).

### 1. Send groups to Ella SMSC

1. Go to **Clients**, open the `smsc` client, and open the **Client scopes** tab.
1. Click `smsc-dedicated`, then **Configure a new mapper**, or **Add mapper** > **By configuration**, then **Group Membership**.
1. Set **Name** and **Token Claim Name** to `groups`. Turn off **Full group path**. Keep **Add to ID token** on.
1. Click **Save**.

The groups are group names, such as `smsc-admins`.

Configure the provider to send the user's groups in a claim, such as `groups`, as a list of group names or IDs.

### 2. Map the groups in Ella SMSC

1. Go to **Single Sign-On** and, in **Roles from groups**, click **Edit**.
1. Set **Groups claim** to `groups`.
1. Click **Add group** for each group, and set the group and its role. Put the most privileged first: a user in several groups gets the role of the first.
1. Click **Update**.

## Pin a user's role

A pinned role is kept whatever the user's groups.

1. Go to **Users** and open the user.
1. In **Account**, edit the role: choose the role, check **Pin role**, and click **Update**. Changing a role that comes from groups checks it for you.

To unpin, uncheck **Pin role**. The role then follows the user's groups from their next login.

## Unlink a user

Unlink a user whose account at the identity provider was replaced, so that their next login links the new account by email.

1. Go to **Users** and open the user.
1. In **Account**, click **Unlink**, then **Unlink**.

## Offboard a user

1. Remove or disable the user at the identity provider. They can no longer sign in, but their current session lasts until the **Session lifetime** ends.
1. To end their access at once, go to **Users** in Ella SMSC, open the user, and click **Delete**. This also deletes their API tokens and [ESMEs](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md).

To keep the user and their ESMEs instead, open the user and:

1. In **Account**, click **Unlink**, then **Unlink**. This ends their single sign-on sessions.
1. Click **Remove Password**, then **Remove**, if they have one.
1. In **API Tokens**, delete each token.

# Perform a Rolling Upgrade

This guide walks through upgrading every node in a running Ella SMSC high-availability cluster, one at a time, without taking the cluster offline.

## Prerequisites

- A running cluster deployed via [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md).
- The next version of `ella-smsc` available.

## Upgrade one node

Repeat these steps for each node.

1. Open the **Cluster** page on any healthy node other than the one you are about to upgrade.

1. In the node's **Node actions** menu, click **Drain this node**. Wait until its **Drain** column shows **Drained**.

1. On that host, refresh the snap:

   ```
   sudo snap refresh ella-smsc
   ```

1. On the **Cluster** page, wait for the node to return to **Healthy**.

1. In the node's **Node actions** menu, click **Resume this node**. Wait until its **Drain** column shows **Active**.

1. Move to the next node.

## Verify the upgrade

After every node has been refreshed, open the **Cluster** page and confirm:

- Every node's **Version** column shows the target release.
- Every node is **Healthy** and its **Drain** column shows **Active**.

# Scale a High Availability Cluster

This guide walks through adding a node to an existing Ella SMSC high-availability cluster, removing one, and replacing one whose database diverged.

## Prerequisites

- A running HA cluster deployed (see [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md)).

## Add a node

1. Prepare a host with Ella SMSC installed per the [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/install/index.md) guide, with a `cluster` block in the configuration file.
1. Open the **Cluster** page on any node in the cluster.
1. Click **Add Node**, click **Create Token**, and copy the token.
1. Start Ella SMSC on the new host.
1. Open the new node's UI in a browser. Click **Join an existing cluster instead**, paste the token, and click **Join**.
1. Connect every Diameter peer to the new node, unless they connect through a Diameter routing agent.
1. On the **Cluster** page, verify the new node appears and is shown as **Healthy**.

## Remove a node

1. Open the **Cluster** page on any node in the cluster.
1. In the node's **Node actions** menu, click **Drain this node**. Wait until its **Drain** column shows **Drained**.
1. In the same menu, click **Remove from cluster**. For a node that is down for good, check **Force remove (skip drain)**.
1. Disconnect the Diameter peers from the removed node.

## Replace a diverged node

A node whose database differs from the leader's shows **Diverged** in the **Healthy** column of the **Cluster** page, and increments `ellasmsc_cluster_state_mismatches_total`.

1. Remove the node, as in [Remove a node](#remove-a-node).

1. On the removed node, stop Ella SMSC and delete its data:

   ```
   sudo snap stop ella-smsc.smscd
   sudo rm -rf /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.db* /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/raft
   sudo snap start ella-smsc.smscd
   ```

1. Add the node back, as in [Add a node](#add-a-node), steps 2, 3, 5 and 6. It gets a new **Diameter Host**.

1. On the **Cluster** page, verify the node is shown as **Healthy**.

# Send Messages from an Application

This guide gives an application, such as an OTA platform, an API token to send messages with.

## 1. Create a user for the application

In the UI, go to **Users** and click **Create**. Set:

- **Email**: an address for the application, such as `ota@example.com`
- **Password**: any password of at least 8 characters
- **Role**: **Submitter**

Click **Create**.

## 2. Create an API token

Open the user, and in **API Tokens**, click **Create Token**. Name it after the application, check **No expiry**, and click **Create**.

Copy the token. It is not shown again.

## 3. Configure the application

Send a message with the token:

```
curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from": "+15550001000", "to": "+15551230002", "text": "hello"}'
```

See the [Messages API](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/messages/index.md).

# Send (U)SIM Data Download Messages over SMPP

This guide connects an OTA platform to Ella SMSC over SMPP 3.4 with TLS, sends a secured packet to a SIM with `submit_sm`, and receives the SIM's answer and a delivery receipt as `deliver_sm`.

## Prerequisites

- **Ella SMSC**: installed, as in [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/install/index.md).
- **A TLS certificate** for the SMSC, `smpp.pem`, with its chain, and its private key, `smpp.key`, in PEM.
- **A user** with the Admin role, logged in to the UI.
- **The OTA platform's network**: the IP prefix it connects from, such as `10.1.0.0/24`.
- **The secured packet**, at most 140 octets with its user data header.

The examples use `15550001000` as the source and `15551230002` as the MSISDN of the SIM.

## 1. Enable the SMPP listener

Copy the certificate and key:

```
sudo cp smpp.pem smpp.key /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/
sudo chmod 600 /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smpp.key
```

In `/var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.yaml`, add:

```
smpp:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 2775
  tls:
    cert: /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smpp.pem
    key: /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smpp.key
```

Restart Ella SMSC:

```
sudo snap restart ella-smsc.smscd
```

## 2. Create a user for the OTA platform

In the UI, go to **Users** and click **Create**. Set:

- **Email**: `ota@example.com`
- **Password**: any password of at least 8 characters
- **Role**: **Submitter**

Click **Create**.

## 3. Add the ESME

Go to **SMPP** and click **Add ESME**. Set:

- **System ID**: `ota`
- **User**: `ota@example.com`
- **Password**: empty, to generate one
- **Allowed networks**: `10.1.0.0/24`

Click **Add**. Copy the generated password from the **ESME Password** dialog. It is not shown again.

## 4. Bind the OTA platform

Configure the OTA platform to bind as a transceiver, with:

| Setting             | Value                         |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Host, port          | `<host-ip>`, `2775`, over TLS |
| `system_id`         | `ota`                         |
| `password`          | The generated password        |
| `interface_version` | `0x34`                        |

On the **SMPP** page, the **Sessions** of `ota` show **Transceiver from** the platform's address.

## 5. Submit the packet

Send a `submit_sm` with:

| Field                                                | Value                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source_addr_ton`, `source_addr_npi`, `source_addr`  | `1`, `1`, `15550001000`                                   |
| `dest_addr_ton`, `dest_addr_npi`, `destination_addr` | `1`, `1`, `15551230002`                                   |
| `esm_class`                                          | `0x40`, UDHI                                              |
| `protocol_id`                                        | `0x7F`, (U)SIM data download                              |
| `data_coding`                                        | `0xF6`, 8-bit data, message class 2                       |
| `registered_delivery`                                | `0x09`: the SIM's answer and a delivery receipt           |
| `short_message`                                      | The packet's user data header, then the packet: `027000…` |

`submit_sm_resp` gives the `message_id`.

## 6. Receive the SIM's answer

The SMSC sends a `deliver_sm` with `esm_class` `0x50` and `receipted_message_id` set to the `message_id`. Its `short_message` is the SIM's Response Packet, `027100…`.

Answer it with `deliver_sm_resp` `ESME_ROK`.

## 7. Receive the delivery receipt

The SMSC sends a `deliver_sm` with `esm_class` `0x04` and `receipted_message_id` set to the `message_id`. Its `short_message` is the receipt:

```
id:42 sub:001 dlvrd:001 submit date:2610281430 done date:2610281431 stat:DELIVRD err:000 text:
```

Answer it with `deliver_sm_resp` `ESME_ROK`.

See the [SMPP reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md) for every field, outcome and refusal.

# Send (U)SIM Data Download Messages over the API

This guide sends a secured packet that an OTA platform built to a SIM, over the HTTP API, and reads the SIM's answer.

## Prerequisites

- **An API token** of a Submitter user, as in [Send Messages from an Application](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/send_messages_from_an_application/index.md).
- **The secured packet**, at most 140 octets with its user data header, in hexadecimal.

## 1. Send the packet

Send the packet as a binary message, with:

- `protocol_identifier`: `127`, (U)SIM data download
- `data_coding_scheme`: `246`, 8-bit data, message class 2
- `user_data_header`: the packet's user data header, such as `027000`
- `user_data`: the packet after its header

```
curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "from": "+15550001000",
        "to": "+15551230002",
        "binary": {
          "protocol_identifier": 127,
          "data_coding_scheme": 246,
          "user_data_header": "027000",
          "user_data": "<packet>"
        }
      }'
```

Note the `id` of the message in the response.

## 2. Wait for the delivery

Get the message until its `status` is no longer `pending`:

```
curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages/<id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..."
```

## 3. Read the SIM's answer

Get the content of the message:

```
curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages/<id>/content \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..."
```

The SIM's answer is the `user_data` of the last item of `deliver_reports`. See [Get the Content of a Message](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/messages/#get-the-content-of-a-message).

- [SMPP](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md)

- [System Requirements](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/system_reqs/index.md)
- [3GPP Compliance](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/3gpp_compliance/index.md)

# 3GPP Compliance

Ella SMSC implements the 3GPP SMSC of TS 23.040, with the S6c, SGd and Gdd Diameter interfaces of TS 29.338.

Note

Open an [issue](https://github.com/ellanetworks/smsc/issues) if you notice a 3GPP-compliance gap or require a new capability for a production deployment.

## Supported

### SGd and Gdd (TS 29.338)

- **MO-Forward-Short-Message**, received: a phone's short message, from its MME, SGSN, SMSF or IP-SM-GW.
- **MT-Forward-Short-Message**, sent: a short message or a status report, to the phone's MME, SGSN, IP-SM-GW, or SMSF for 3GPP or non-3GPP access.

### S6c (TS 29.338)

- **Send-Routing-Info-for-SM**, sent: the serving nodes of the recipient, for a short message or a status report.
- **Report-SM-Delivery-Status**, sent: the outcome of a delivery, which sets or clears the HSS's message waiting data.
- **Alert-Service-Centre**, received: the recipient, or the Alert MSISDN of its subscription, can be reached again.

### Diameter routing (RFC 6733, GSMA IR.88)

- **Static peers.** Over SCTP, multi-homed.
- **Realm routing.** Per realm and application, with a default route, and Destination-Host kept.
- **Failover.** By priority, with load sharing, and the T flag on retransmission.

### Short messages (TS 23.040)

- **TPDUs.** SMS-SUBMIT received; SMS-DELIVER and SMS-STATUS-REPORT sent; SMS-SUBMIT-REPORT with the TP-Failure-Cause of a refused SMS-SUBMIT.
- **Store and forward.** Messages to a phone are delivered in order, one at a time, and announce the next with TP-More-Messages-to-Send.
- **Validity period.** Relative, absolute and enhanced formats, including single-shot messages.
- **Status reports.** On the delivery, failure, expiry or replacement of a message whose sender set TP-Status-Report-Request.
- **Reject duplicates.** TP-Reject-Duplicates.
- **Replace short message.** Replace types 1 to 7 of TP-Protocol-Identifier, from phones, the API and SMPP. A message replaces only one from the same submitter: a phone's, one from the same phone (TS 23.040 §2.1.1); the API's or an ESME's, one of the same user or ESME.
- **Binary messages from the API and SMPP.** TP-Protocol-Identifier, TP-Data-Coding-Scheme, TP-User-Data-Header and TP-User-Data delivered unchanged, including (U)SIM data download.
- **SMS-DELIVER-REPORT.** Kept from each delivery: in the SM-RP-UI of a successful MT-Forward-Short-Message answer, and in the SM-Diagnostic-Info of an SM Delivery Failure.
- **(U)SIM data download error.** A message whose SMS-DELIVER-REPORT has the TP-Failure-Cause `usim_data_download_error` fails without another attempt.
- **SC time stamps.** Distinct for the messages to a phone.
- **Numbering.** International, national and unknown types of number, converted to international with the operator's numbering plan.

## Not supported

- **SMS-COMMAND.** Refused with the TP-Failure-Cause `command_unsupported`.
- **Telematic interworking.** Refused with the TP-Failure-Cause `telematic_interworking_not_supported`.
- **Device triggering from phones.** Refused with the TP-Failure-Cause `unspecified_tp_pid_error`.
- **SMSMI-Correlation-ID.** A short message that carries one is refused with DIAMETER_ERROR_FACILITY_NOT_SUPPORTED.
- **Diameter over TCP.**
- **Delivery to an MSC-Number.**
- **Destination-Host in Report-SM-Delivery-Status.**
- **MAP over SS7.**
- **Routing to other networks' HSSs.** Send-Routing-Info-for-SM goes to the operator's realm only, not the realm of the recipient's MSISDN (TS 29.338 §5.3.1.1.2).

# Configuration File

Ella SMSC is configured using a YAML file. Start Ella SMSC with the `--config` flag to specify its path. Unknown keys are rejected. Changes take effect on restart.

The operator and delivery settings are not in this file: they are in the database, and set with the UI or the [API](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/index.md).

## Parameters

- `logging` (object, optional): The logging configuration.
  - `level` (string, optional): The log level: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, or `error`. Default `info`.
- `db` (object): The database configuration.
  - `path` (string): The path to the SQLite database file. Created if absent.
- `api` (object): The HTTP API and UI.
  - `address` (string): The IP address to listen on. `0.0.0.0` or `::` for all addresses.
  - `port` (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default `5010`.
  - `tls` (object, optional): Serve over HTTPS. Default: plain HTTP.
    - `cert` (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
    - `key` (string): The path to the PEM private key.
- `diameter` (object): Diameter, to the HSS, MMEs, SMSFs and IP-SM-GWs.
  - `name` (string): The network interface to listen on, on all its addresses, advertised to peers. Either `name` or `address` must be set.
  - `address` (string): The IP address to listen on, advertised to peers. A specific address, not `0.0.0.0` or `::`. Either `name` or `address` must be set.
  - `port` (int, optional): The SCTP port to listen on. Default `3868`.
- `smpp` (object, optional): The [SMPP 3.4](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md) listener for ESMEs, such as OTA platforms. Without it, Ella SMSC does not listen for SMPP. The ESME accounts are in the database, managed with the [API](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md).
  - `address` (string): The IP address to listen on. `0.0.0.0` or `::` for all addresses.
  - `port` (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default `2775`. Not the API's port.
  - `tls` (object, optional): Wrap each connection in TLS, 1.2 or later, from its first octet. SMPP 3.4 has no TLS: this is a common convention, which the ESME must support. Default: plain TCP, for a private link or a lab only.
    - `cert` (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
    - `key` (string): The path to the PEM private key.
- `cluster` (object, optional): The cluster port. Required to create or join a [cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/explanation/high_availability/index.md).
  - `address` (string): The IP address to listen on. `0.0.0.0` or `::` for all addresses, with `advertise` set.
  - `port` (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default `7000`.
  - `advertise` (string, optional): The `host:port` the other nodes reach this node at. Default `address:port`.
- `telemetry` (object, optional): The [traces](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/observability/#traces).
  - `enabled` (boolean, optional): Export traces. Default `false`.
  - `otlp_endpoint` (string): The `host:port` of an OTLP/gRPC collector, over plain gRPC. Required when `enabled` is `true`.

## Example

```
logging:
  level: info
db:
  path: smsc.db
api:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 5010
diameter:
  address: 127.0.0.1
  port: 3868
cluster:
  address: 10.0.0.1
  port: 7000
smpp:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 2775
  tls:
    cert: /etc/smsc/smpp.pem
    key: /etc/smsc/smpp.key
telemetry:
  enabled: true
  otlp_endpoint: localhost:4317
```

With the snap, the configuration file is `/var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.yaml`.

# Connectivity

| Interface                                                              | Peer                                                                                                   | Transport                   | Address                                                 | Port                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| API and UI                                                             | Operators, applications, Prometheus                                                                    | TCP                         | `api.address`                                           | `api.port` (`5010`)        |
| Diameter: S6c                                                          | HSS                                                                                                    | SCTP                        | `diameter.address`, or the addresses of `diameter.name` | `diameter.port` (`3868`)   |
| Diameter: SGd and Gdd                                                  | MME, SMSF, IP-SM-GW over SGd; SGSN over Gdd                                                            | SCTP                        | `diameter.address`, or the addresses of `diameter.name` | `diameter.port` (`3868`)   |
| Diameter: S6c and SGd, outbound                                        | [Configured peers](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/diameter/#create-a-peer): DEA, DRA | SCTP                        | The peer's `addresses`                                  | The peer's `port` (`3868`) |
| [SMPP 3.4](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md) | ESMEs, such as OTA platforms                                                                           | TCP, or TLS with `smpp.tls` | `smpp.address`                                          | `smpp.port` (`2775`)       |
| Cluster                                                                | The other Ella SMSC nodes                                                                              | TCP, mutual TLS 1.3         | `cluster.address`, advertised as `cluster.advertise`    | `cluster.port` (`7000`)    |

Defaults are in parentheses. SMPP listens only when the configuration file has an `smpp` block, and the cluster port only when it has a `cluster` block.

Ella SMSC accepts any Diameter peer that supports S6c or SGd. It connects to the configured peers, and reconnects after 1 to 30 seconds. In a cluster, every node connects to the configured peers, and every other peer connects to every node.

## Diameter identity

| Item  | Value                                                  |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Host  | `smsc-<id>.node.epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org` |
| Realm | `epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org`                |

`<MCC>` and `<MNC>` are the operator's, with a 2-digit MNC padded to 3. `<id>` is the last 12 hex characters of the node ID. The host does not change for the life of the node.

# Observability

Ella SMSC supports four observability pillars: Metrics, Logs, Traces, and Profiles.

## Metrics

Ella SMSC exposes Prometheus metrics at [`GET /api/v1/metrics`](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/metrics/index.md).

| Metric                                       | Type                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ellasmsc_build_info`                        | Gauge                   | Always 1. The version and revision of the running build are in its labels.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `ellasmsc_messages_received_total`           | Counter                 | Short messages received, one per part, by origin (`mobile`, `api`, `smpp`) and result (`accepted`, `rejected`, `error`, and `throttled` for `smpp`). One per `submit_sm` for `smpp`, `throttled` when the [inbound window](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md) is full. |
| `ellasmsc_messages_completed_total`          | Counter                 | Short messages and status reports that reached a final status, by type (`message`, `status_report`) and status (`delivered`, `failed`, `expired`, and `replaced` for a message).                                                                                                                |
| `ellasmsc_messages_purged_total`             | Counter                 | Short messages deleted once their [retention](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/retention/index.md) passed, with their status reports and delivery attempts.                                                                                                                     |
| `ellasmsc_messages_pending`                  | Gauge                   | Short messages and status reports waiting for delivery, by type and state: `due`, to be delivered now or being delivered; `waiting`, for a retry or for the phone to be reachable. Exported by the leader only.                                                                                 |
| `ellasmsc_message_delivery_duration_seconds` | Histogram               | Time from submission to delivery of the short messages delivered, the time the phone was unreachable included.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ellasmsc_hss_peers`                         | Gauge                   | Open peers that serve S6c in the operator's realm: HSSs, or agents in front of them. At 0, messages to phones wait.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `ellasmsc_peer_requests_total`               | Counter                 | Requests to the HSS and to the MMEs, SMSFs and IP-SM-GWs, by interface (`s6c`, `sgd`) and result (`success`, `failure`, `absent_user`, `error`, `timeout`).                                                                                                                                     |
| `ellasmsc_peer_request_duration_seconds`     | Histogram               | Duration of requests to the HSS and to the MMEs, SMSFs and IP-SM-GWs, by interface.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `ellasmsc_smpp_sessions`                     | Gauge                   | Bound SMPP sessions, by bind type (`transmitter`, `receiver`, `transceiver`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ellasmsc_smpp_binds_total`                  | Counter                 | SMPP bind attempts, by result (`accepted`, `rejected`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `ellasmsc_smpp_notifications_pending`        | Gauge                   | Delivery receipts and SIM answers not yet sent to an ESME and not expired, by type (`receipt`, `sim_answer`). A rise means no receiver of the ESME is bound, or it does not acknowledge them. Exported by the leader only.                                                                      |
| `ellasmsc_smpp_notifications_sent_total`     | Counter                 | Delivery receipts and SIM answers that reached a final outcome, by type and result (`acknowledged`, `rejected`, `expired`, `no_user_data`).                                                                                                                                                     |
| `ellasmsc_smpp_submit_duration_seconds`      | Histogram               | Time from a `submit_sm` read to its `submit_sm_resp` written.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ellasmsc_api_request_duration_seconds`      | Histogram               | Duration of API requests, by method, route (`/api/v1/messages/{id}`) and status code. Requests to `/api/v1/pprof/` and to no route are left out.                                                                                                                                                |
| `ellasmsc_oidc_logins_total`                 | Counter                 | Logins through the identity provider, by outcome: `success`, or a [login error](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/auth/#errors).                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ellasmsc_database_query_duration_seconds`   | Histogram               | Duration of database calls, the wait for the connection included.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `ellasmsc_database_query_errors_total`       | Counter                 | Failed database calls.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ellasmsc_database_storage_bytes`            | Gauge                   | Size of the database on disk, by file: `main`, `wal`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `ellasmsc_cluster_failure_tolerance`         | Gauge                   | Voters that can fail without stopping writes. Leader only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `ellasmsc_cluster_state_mismatches_total`    | Counter                 | Members whose database differs from the leader's.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `go_*`                                       | Gauge, Counter, Summary | Go runtime: goroutines, heap, garbage-collection pauses.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `process_*`                                  | Gauge, Counter          | Process: memory, CPU, open file descriptors, start time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `raft_*`                                     | Gauge, Counter, Summary | [hashicorp/raft](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft) metrics. In a cluster only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Traces

Ella SMSC exports [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) traces when `telemetry.enabled` is set in the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/config_file/index.md).

| Property                          | Value                                               |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Export                            | OTLP over gRPC, without TLS                         |
| Sampling                          | Parent-based, always on for a trace the SMSC starts |
| Propagation                       | W3C Trace Context                                   |
| Delivery, SMPP and Diameter spans | No MSISDN, IMSI or message content                  |

### Spans

| Span                             | Kind           | Description                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{method} {route}`               | Server         | A request to the API, except `/api/v1/livez`, `/api/v1/readyz`, `/api/v1/metrics` and `/api/v1/pprof/`. Links to the caller's `traceparent`.                        |
| `submit_sm`                      | Server         | A `submit_sm` from an ESME.                                                                                                                                         |
| `deliver {origin_host}`          | Consumer       | A delivery attempt of a short message or status report, named after the Diameter Origin-Host of the SMSC. A new trace, linked to the span that created the message. |
| `deliver_sm`                     | Client         | A delivery receipt or SIM answer to an ESME. A new trace, linked to the span that created the message.                                                              |
| `S6c/{command}`, `SGd/{command}` | Server, Client | A Diameter request.                                                                                                                                                 |

### Attributes

| Attribute                   | Span                    | Values                                                               |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ella.sms.delivery.outcome` | `deliver {origin_host}` | `delivered`, `failed`, `expired`, `replaced`, `retry`, `interrupted` |

## Profiles

Ella SMSC exposes the [net/http/pprof](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http/pprof) API at [`/api/v1/pprof/`](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/pprof/index.md).

## Logs

Ella SMSC writes its logs to standard output, one JSON object per line, at the level of `logging.level` in the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/config_file/index.md).

| Field         | Description                                                                              |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ts`          | Time of the event.                                                                       |
| `level`       | `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`.                                                      |
| `msg`         | What happened.                                                                           |
| `trace_id`    | Trace ID of the span the event happened in, as 32 hex digits. Absent outside a span.     |
| `span_id`     | Span ID of the span the event happened in, as 16 hex digits. Absent outside a span.      |
| `trace_flags` | W3C trace flags of that span, as 2 hex digits: `01` when sampled. Absent outside a span. |

Other fields depend on the event.

### Audit events

Audit events are logs at level `info` with `msg` set to `audit event`.

| Field     | Description                                       |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `action`  | What was done, below.                             |
| `actor`   | Email of the user who did it. Empty when unknown. |
| `ip`      | Address the request came from.                    |
| `details` | What was done, in words.                          |

# Performance

Measured short message capacity of Ella SMSC, with 100,000 subscribers, on 1 node and on a 3-node [cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/explanation/high_availability/index.md), each node on 4 CPU cores.

Ella SMSC sustains 2,000 short messages per second from phones, on 1 node or a 3-node cluster, with every message delivered and a delivery p99 under 120 ms.

## Short Messages from Phones

Submission time: from the MO-Forward-Short-Message request to its answer, the message accepted and stored. Delivery time: from the MO-Forward-Short-Message request to the MT-Forward-Short-Message request of its delivery to the recipient's MME (TS 29.338 §6.2).

### 1 Node

| Rate (/s) | Messages per hour | Submission success rate | Submission time, p99 | Delivery success rate | Delivery time, mean | Delivery time, p99 | CPU (cores) |
| --------- | ----------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------ | ----------- |
| 500       | 1,800,000         | 100%                    | 33 ms                | 100%                  | 34 ms               | 59 ms              | 0.26        |
| 1,000     | 3,600,000         | 100%                    | 34 ms                | 100%                  | 32 ms               | 59 ms              | 0.40        |
| 1,500     | 5,400,000         | 100%                    | 39 ms                | 100%                  | 36 ms               | 68 ms              | 0.53        |
| 2,000     | 7,200,000         | 100%                    | 49 ms                | 100%                  | 41 ms               | 81 ms              | 0.68        |

### 3 Nodes

| Rate (/s) | Messages per hour | Submission success rate | Submission time, p99 | Delivery success rate | Delivery time, mean | Delivery time, p99 | CPU of the leader (cores) |
| --------- | ----------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------- |
| 500       | 1,800,000         | 100%                    | 90 ms                | 100%                  | 75 ms               | 135 ms             | 0.24                      |
| 1,000     | 3,600,000         | 100%                    | 67 ms                | 100%                  | 65 ms               | 96 ms              | 0.40                      |
| 1,500     | 5,400,000         | 100%                    | 75 ms                | 100%                  | 68 ms               | 108 ms             | 0.56                      |
| 2,000     | 7,200,000         | 100%                    | 79 ms                | 100%                  | 71 ms               | 113 ms             | 0.72                      |

## Short Messages from ESMEs

Submission time: from the `submit_sm` to its `submit_sm_resp`, the message accepted and stored. Delivery time: from the `submit_sm` to the MT-Forward-Short-Message request of its delivery to the recipient's MME (TS 29.338 §6.2).

### Without Delivery Receipts

| Nodes | Rate (/s) | Rate reached (/s) | Submission time, p99 | Delivery time, mean | Delivery time, p99 | CPU (cores) | Resident memory |
| ----- | --------- | ----------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------ | ----------- | --------------- |
| 1     | 1,000     | 1,000             | 33 ms                | 33 ms               | 58 ms              | 0.39        | 71 MiB          |
| 1     | 2,000     | 1,998             | 283 ms               | 86 ms               | 304 ms             | 0.62        | 71 MiB          |
| 3     | 1,000     | 999               | 75 ms                | 67 ms               | 115 ms             | 0.39        | 83 MiB          |
| 3     | 2,000     | 1,170             | 14.0 s               | 6.90 s              | 14.0 s             | 0.41        | 135 MiB         |

### With Delivery Receipts

Receipt time: from the `submit_sm` to the `deliver_sm` of its delivery receipt.

| Nodes | Rate (/s) | Submission time, p99 | Delivery time, mean | Delivery time, p99 | Receipt time, mean | Receipt time, p99 | CPU (cores) | Resident memory |
| ----- | --------- | -------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------ | ----------------- | ----------- | --------------- |
| 1     | 600       | 34 ms                | 34 ms               | 61 ms              | 58 ms              | 97 ms             | 0.35        | 57 MiB          |
| 1     | 1,200     | 42 ms                | 37 ms               | 74 ms              | 2.10 s             | 4.33 s            | 0.54        | 90 MiB          |
| 3     | 600       | 64 ms                | 67 ms               | 121 ms             | 1.53 s             | 2.96 s            | 0.31        | 82 MiB          |
| 3     | 1,200     | 113 ms               | 81 ms               | 148 ms             | 10.2 s             | 18.2 s            | 0.52        | 99 MiB          |

Every message was submitted, delivered and receipted.

In a cluster, CPU and memory are those of the node the ESME is bound to.

## Test Setup

| Item                       | Value                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Version                    | Ella SMSC built from source, after v0.0.1, default configuration, with the SMPP listener                                                               |
| Host                       | 1 host: Intel Core Ultra 7 265K, 20 cores, NVMe SSD with ext4, Ubuntu 26.04, Linux 7.0                                                                 |
| Nodes                      | Each pinned to its own 4 cores, on its own loopback address. The nodes of a cluster share the SSD.                                                     |
| Load generator             | On the same host, pinned to 8 other cores                                                                                                              |
| Core network               | Simulated MME and HSS, over SGd and S6c, over SCTP, connected to every node: answers at once                                                           |
| Subscribers                | 100,000, all reachable                                                                                                                                 |
| Short messages from phones | SMS-SUBMIT of 8-bit text, 25 to 30 octets, without status report requests, each from a subscriber to another at random, spread over every node         |
| ESME                       | 1, with 4 transceiver sessions to one node, at most 10 `submit_sm` without a response per session                                                      |
| Short messages from ESMEs  | `submit_sm` of 8-bit data, `data_coding` `0x04`, 12 to 17 octets, each to a subscriber at random. With delivery receipts: `registered_delivery` `0x01` |
| Rates                      | Each held 20 s, in increasing order, on a new database for each table                                                                                  |
| Runs                       | 1 of each table                                                                                                                                        |
| Success                    | Delivered, or receipted, within 20 s of the end of the rate                                                                                            |

# SMPP

Ella SMSC is an SMPP 3.4 SMSC for External Short Message Entities (ESMEs), such as OTA platforms. An ESME submits short messages to phones with `submit_sm`, and receives delivery receipts and SIM answers as `deliver_sm`.

The listener runs when the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/config_file/index.md) has an `smpp` block. ESME accounts are managed with the [ESMEs API](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md) or the **SMPP** page of the UI.

"§" without a TS number refers to SMPP v3.4, Issue 1.2. **Convention** marks a behaviour that SMPP 3.4 does not define. All conventions are listed under [Conventions](#conventions).

## Transport

| Item                | Value                                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Transport           | TCP (§2.4), on `smpp.port`, default `2775`.                                                                 |
| TLS                 | With `smpp.tls`: TLS 1.2 or later, from the first octet. A listener is either plain or TLS. **Convention**. |
| Client address      | The address of the TCP connection. The PROXY protocol is not supported.                                     |
| `interface_version` | `0x34`.                                                                                                     |
| SMSC `system_id`    | `EllaSMSC`, in bind responses.                                                                              |
| `command_length`    | 16 to 69,632 octets (68 KiB). **Convention**: SMPP 3.4 sets no maximum (§3.2.1).                            |
| `sequence_number`   | `0x00000001` to `0x7FFFFFFF` (§5.1.4).                                                                      |

## PDUs

### Supported

| PDU                                                     | Direction   | Session state       | Handling                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bind_transmitter`, `bind_receiver`, `bind_transceiver` | ESME → SMSC | OPEN                | See [Binds](#binds).                                                                                     |
| `submit_sm`                                             | ESME → SMSC | BOUND_TX, BOUND_TRX | One short message. See [`submit_sm`](#submit_sm).                                                        |
| `deliver_sm`                                            | SMSC → ESME | BOUND_RX, BOUND_TRX | Delivery receipts and SIM answers. See [Notifications](#notifications).                                  |
| `enquire_link`                                          | Both        | Bound               | Answered at once (§4.11).                                                                                |
| `unbind`                                                | Both        | Bound               | See [Session end](#session-end).                                                                         |
| `generic_nack`                                          | Both        | Any                 | Sent for a PDU that cannot be handled (§4.3). Received in answer to a `deliver_sm`: a temporary failure. |

### Errors

| PDU received                                                                                                                     | Response                                                 | Session  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `command_length` under 16 or over 68 KiB                                                                                         | `generic_nack` `ESME_RINVCMDLEN`                         | Closed   |
| `sequence_number` of `0` or over `0x7FFFFFFF`                                                                                    | `generic_nack` `ESME_RUNKNOWNERR`, `sequence_number` `0` | Stays up |
| `query_sm`, `replace_sm`, `cancel_sm`, `submit_multi`, `data_sm`, `outbind`, `deliver_sm`, an undefined or reserved `command_id` | `generic_nack` `ESME_RINVCMDID`                          | Stays up |
| `alert_notification`                                                                                                             | None: discarded (§4.12)                                  | Stays up |
| A bind in a bound state                                                                                                          | Its response with `ESME_RALYBND`                         | Stays up |
| Another request in a state that does not allow it (§2.3, Table 2-1)                                                              | Its response with `ESME_RINVBNDSTS`                      | Stays up |
| A body on a PDU that has none, or a body shorter than its mandatory parameters                                                   | `generic_nack` `ESME_RINVCMDLEN`                         | Stays up |
| A C-Octet String over its maximum length                                                                                         | Its response with `ESME_RINVPARLEN`                      | Stays up |
| Optional parameters that do not decode as TLVs                                                                                   | Its response with `ESME_RINVOPTPARSTREAM`                | Stays up |
| A response that matches no request                                                                                               | None: discarded                                          | Stays up |

Unknown TLVs, and known TLVs not expected for the PDU, are ignored (§3.3). Responses may go out of order: they match their requests by `sequence_number` (§2.5.2).

## Binds

### Checks

The SMSC checks a bind in this order:

1. At most 20 binds per minute from the client address: per IPv4 address, or per IPv6 /64.

1. `interface_version` is `0x34` or later.

1. At most 100 wrong passwords per hour for the `system_id`, from inside its allowed networks. A successful bind resets the count. Wrong passwords from outside the allowed networks, and binds with an unknown `system_id`, are counted apart, with the same limit, and never lock out the account.

1. `system_id` and `password` match an ESME account. A check against an unknown `system_id` takes as long as one against a known `system_id`.

1. The client address is in the account's `allowed_networks`. An empty list allows no address.

1. The role of the account's user allows the bind type:

   | Bind        | Permissions                     | Roles                             |
   | ----------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
   | Transmitter | Send messages                   | Admin, Network Manager, Submitter |
   | Receiver    | Read messages and their content | Admin, Network Manager, Submitter |
   | Transceiver | Both                            | Admin, Network Manager, Submitter |

   See [Roles](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/#roles).

1. Fewer than 4 sessions of the account are bound.

### Response

| Outcome            | `command_status`                                             | Body                                                                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Accepted           | `ESME_ROK`                                                   | `system_id` `EllaSMSC`, and `sc_interface_version` `0x34` (§5.3.2.25). |
| Refused, any check | `ESME_RBINDFAIL`, never `ESME_RINVSYSID` or `ESME_RINVPASWD` | None. `bind_transceiver_resp`: `system_id` `EllaSMSC` (Table 4-6).     |

The log gives the reason of a refused bind, with the `system_id` and the client address, at level `info`.

### Bind fields

| Field                                                  | Handling                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- |
| `system_id`                                            | Up to 15 characters (§4.1.1). |
| `password`                                             | Up to 8 characters (§4.1.1).  |
| `interface_version`                                    | See [Checks](#checks).        |
| `system_type`, `addr_ton`, `addr_npi`, `address_range` | Ignored.                      |

### Account changes

Updating or deleting an ESME, or changing the role of or deleting its user, closes its sessions.

## Sessions

### Limits

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sessions per ESME | 4, of any bind types.                                                                                                      |
| ESME accounts     | 50.                                                                                                                        |
| Inbound window    | 64 requests handled at once per session. One more is answered `ESME_RTHROTTLED`. §2.5.2 recommends at most 10 outstanding. |
| Outbound window   | 10 `deliver_sm` without a response per session (§2.6.2).                                                                   |

### Timers

The timers are fixed (§7.2).

| Timer                | Value                       | Action                                                                                                |
| -------------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `session_init_timer` | 30 s                        | A connection that has not bound is closed.                                                            |
| `enquire_link_timer` | 30 s without a PDU received | The SMSC sends `enquire_link`, and closes the session without a response within the `response_timer`. |
