| `inactivity_timer`   | 90 s without a PDU received | The session is closed.                                                                                |
| `response_timer`     | 30 s                        | A `deliver_sm` without a response is a temporary failure.                                             |

### Session end

| Event                  | Handling                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `unbind` from the ESME | The SMSC finishes the `submit_sm` in progress, answers `unbind_resp`, waits up to 2 s for the ESME to close the connection, then closes it (§2.2, §4.2). A `submit_sm` received meanwhile is answered `ESME_RINVBNDSTS`. |
| SMSC shutdown          | The SMSC sends `unbind` to each session, waits up to 5 s for `unbind_resp`, then closes.                                                                                                                                 |

## `submit_sm`

One `submit_sm` stores exactly one SMS-SUBMIT: one message of the [Messages API](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/messages/index.md), owned by the ESME's user, delivered as a message from the API.

`submit_sm_resp` carries `message_id`: the `id` of the message in the Messages API, in decimal. The SMSC answers once the message is stored.

### Addressing

The destination is a phone, routed through the HSS (§5.2.5, §5.2.6, §5.2.9; TS 23.040 §9.1.2.5):

| `dest_addr_ton`                | `dest_addr_npi` | `destination_addr`                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `1`, international             | `0` or `1`      | The international number.                                                                                                            |
| `0`, unknown, or `2`, national | `0` or `1`      | Converted to international with the operator's [numbering plan](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/operator/index.md). |

| Error                                                                              | `command_status`  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| Another `dest_addr_ton`                                                            | `ESME_RINVDSTTON` |
| Another `dest_addr_npi`                                                            | `ESME_RINVDSTNPI` |
| Not 1 to 20 digits, or not 1 to 15 digits without a leading `0` once international | `ESME_RINVDSTADR` |

The source is shown to the recipient as the sender (§5.2.8):

| `source_addr_ton`         | `source_addr_npi`                    | `source_addr`                                                           | Sent to the phone as  |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `1`, international        | `0` or `1`                           | 1 to 15 digits, no leading `0`                                          | TON 1, NPI 1          |
| `5`, alphanumeric         | Any                                  | 1 to 11 letters and digits, single spaces between words, not all digits | TON 5                 |
| `0`, `2`, `3`, `4` or `6` | `0`, `1`, `3`, `4`, `8`, `9` or `10` | 1 to 20 digits                                                          | The TON and NPI given |

| Error                        | `command_status`                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Empty `source_addr`          | `ESME_RINVSRCADR`. The SMSC has no default source.                                                     |
| A reserved `source_addr_ton` | `ESME_RINVSRCTON`                                                                                      |
| Another `source_addr_npi`    | `ESME_RINVSRCNPI`. The NPIs accepted have the same value and meaning in §5.2.6 and TS 23.040 §9.1.2.5. |
| Another `source_addr`        | `ESME_RINVSRCADR`                                                                                      |

### `data_coding`

`data_coding` (§5.2.19) is mapped to a TP-DCS (TS 23.038 §4):

| `data_coding`                                                          | SMPP 3.4 meaning                  | TP-DCS and user data                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0x00`                                                                 | SMSC default alphabet             | TP-DCS `0x00`. The octets are GSM 7-bit default alphabet septets, one per octet, `0x1B` for the extension table. An octet over `0x7F`: `ESME_RSUBMITFAIL`. **Convention**. |
| `0x01`                                                                 | IA5 (ASCII)                       | Converted to GSM 7-bit, TP-DCS `0x00`, or to UCS2, TP-DCS `0x08`, when a character has no GSM 7-bit equivalent. An octet over `0x7F`: `ESME_RSUBMITFAIL`.                  |
| `0x02`                                                                 | Octet unspecified                 | TP-DCS `0x04`, 8-bit.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `0x03`                                                                 | Latin-1                           | Converted to GSM 7-bit, TP-DCS `0x00`, or to UCS2, TP-DCS `0x08`, when a character has no GSM 7-bit equivalent.                                                            |
| `0x04`                                                                 | Octet unspecified                 | TP-DCS `0x04`, 8-bit.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `0x08`                                                                 | UCS2                              | TP-DCS `0x08`, octets copied. An odd number of octets: `ESME_RSUBMITFAIL`.                                                                                                 |
| `0xF0` to `0xF7`                                                       | GSM message class control         | Copied.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `0xC0` to `0xDF`                                                       | GSM message waiting indication    | `ESME_RSUBMITFAIL`.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `0x05` to `0x07`, `0x09` to `0xBF`, `0xE0` to `0xEF`, `0xF8` to `0xFF` | Other character sets, or reserved | `ESME_RSUBMITFAIL`. SMPP 3.4 has no status for an invalid `data_coding`.                                                                                                   |

With a GSM 7-bit TP-DCS, the SMSC packs the septets after the user data header, with fill bits (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24).

**`dest_addr_subunit`** (§5.3.2.1, §5.2.19 note e) sets the message class bits of TP-DCS:

| `dest_addr_subunit`   | Class      |
| --------------------- | ---------- |
| `0`, `5` to `255`     | Unchanged. |
| `1`, MS display       | Class 0    |
| `2`, mobile equipment | Class 1    |
| `3`, smart card       | Class 2    |
| `4`, external unit    | Class 3    |

A different class already in `data_coding`, or a TP-DCS without class bits: `ESME_RINVOPTPARAMVAL`.

**(U)SIM data download.** With `protocol_id` `0x7F`, `data_coding` `0x02` or `0x04` and no `dest_addr_subunit`, TP-DCS is `0xF6`, 8-bit data, class 2. **Convention**: TS 23.040 §9.2.3.9 requires class 2 for (U)SIM data download.

### `esm_class`

| Bits (§5.2.12)      | Value                                 | Handling                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1-0, messaging mode | `00` default, `11` store and forward  | Store and forward.                                                                                                                              |
| 1-0                 | `01` datagram, `10` transaction       | `ESME_RINVESMCLASS`                                                                                                                             |
| 5-2, message type   | `0010`, `0100`, ESME acknowledgements | `ESME_RINVESMCLASS`                                                                                                                             |
| 5-2                 | Other                                 | Normal message (§3.3).                                                                                                                          |
| 6, UDHI             | `1`                                   | TP-UDHI = 1. The user data starts with the user data header, its length octet included. A header longer than the user data: `ESME_RSUBMITFAIL`. |
| 7, reply path       | `1`                                   | `ESME_RINVESMCLASS`                                                                                                                             |

### `protocol_id`

Copied to TP-PID (§5.2.13; TS 23.040 §9.2.3.9):

| `protocol_id`                                        | Handling                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0x20` to `0x3E`, telematic interworking             | `ESME_RSUBMITFAIL`                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `0x41` to `0x47`, replace short message types 1 to 7 | Replaces the pending message of the same type, from the same source, submitted by the same ESME. A message from a phone, the API or another ESME is never replaced. **Convention**. |
| `0x48`, device triggering                            | Needs an application port addressing information element, else `ESME_RSUBMITFAIL`.                                                                                                  |
| `0x7C`, `0x7F`                                       | Need message class 2 after the `data_coding` mapping, else `ESME_RSUBMITFAIL`.                                                                                                      |
| Other                                                | Copied.                                                                                                                                                                             |

### `registered_delivery`

`registered_delivery` (§5.2.17) asks for notifications to the ESME. It does not set TP-Status-Report-Request.

| Bits | Value                                         | Handling                                                      |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1-0  | `00`                                          | No receipt.                                                   |
| 1-0  | `01`                                          | A [receipt](#delivery-receipts) on the final status.          |
| 1-0  | `10`                                          | A receipt on failure only: `failed`, `expired` or `replaced`. |
| 1-0  | `11`                                          | Reserved: no receipt (§3.3).                                  |
| 3-2  | `10` or `11`, SME Manual/User Acknowledgement | The [SIM answer](#sim-answers).                               |
| 3-2  | `01`, SME Delivery Acknowledgement            | Accepted, not honoured.                                       |
| 4    | `1`, intermediate notification                | Accepted, not honoured.                                       |

### Validity and scheduling

| Field                    | Handling                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `validity_period`        | Empty: the default validity of the [delivery settings](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/delivery/index.md). Absolute or relative (§7.1.1): the end of the validity period. In the past or malformed: `ESME_RINVEXPIRY`. The SMS-DELIVER carries no validity period. |
| `schedule_delivery_time` | Not empty: `ESME_RINVSCHED`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

A two-digit year is read within 49 years before and 50 years after the current year. **Convention**.

### User data and optional parameters

| Field                                                         | Handling                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `short_message` (§5.2.22), `message_payload` (§5.3.2.32)      | One or the other. Both: `ESME_ROPTPARNOTALLWD`.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `sm_length`                                                   | Must match `short_message`. `255`, or a mismatch: `ESME_RINVMSGLEN`.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| User data                                                     | Must fit one TPDU once mapped: 140 octets, or 160 septets, the user data header included. Else `ESME_RINVMSGLEN`. The SMSC does not split user data.                                                                                            |
| `sar_msg_ref_num`, `sar_total_segments`, `sar_segment_seqnum` | All three: a concatenation information element, `0x00` with a reference up to 255, else `0x08` (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24.1, §9.2.3.24.8). Not all three: ignored. A total of 0, or a sequence number of 0 or over the total: `ESME_RINVOPTPARAMVAL`. |
| `source_port`, `destination_port`                             | A 16-bit application port addressing information element, `0x05` (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24.4). A missing one of the two is port 0. **Convention**.                                                                                                   |
| `sar_*` or ports with UDHI set                                | `ESME_ROPTPARNOTALLWD` (§5.2.12).                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `user_message_reference`                                      | Echoed in the receipt and the SIM answer.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `sm_default_msg_id`                                           | `1` to `254`: `ESME_RINVDFTMSGID`. The SMSC has no canned messages.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `replace_if_present_flag`                                     | `1`: `ESME_RINVSUBREP`. Other values: taken as `0`.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `service_type`, `priority_flag`, other optional parameters    | Ignored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

### Order of `submit_sm_resp` and `deliver_sm`

The message is handed to delivery once `submit_sm_resp` is written. A notification on the message can still reach the ESME before its `submit_sm_resp` when another message to the same recipient is being delivered.

## Notifications

When a message from an ESME reaches its final status, the SMSC queues the SIM answer, then the receipt, that the `submit_sm` asked for, and sends them as `deliver_sm`.

| Item                                                                                         | Handling                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Session                                                                                      | A receiver or transceiver session of the ESME that submitted the message, the one with the fewest `deliver_sm` in flight. **Convention**.                                                  |
| No receiving session                                                                         | Notifications wait until the ESME binds as receiver or transceiver. They survive a restart.                                                                                                |
| Order                                                                                        | Notifications on one message go one at a time: the receipt waits until the SIM answer is acknowledged, rejected or expired.                                                                |
| `deliver_sm_resp` `ESME_ROK`                                                                 | Acknowledged.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `deliver_sm_resp` `ESME_RX_P_APPN` or `ESME_RX_R_APPN`                                       | Rejected. Not sent again.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ESME_RX_T_APPN`, another status, `generic_nack`, or no response within the `response_timer` | Sent again after 1 minute, then doubling, at most every hour.                                                                                                                              |
| Session closed or unbinding during the send                                                  | Sent again at once on another receiving session, or on the next bind.                                                                                                                      |
| Expiry                                                                                       | The default validity of the [delivery settings](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/delivery/index.md), from the message's final status. An expired notification is not sent. |
| ESME deleted                                                                                 | Its notifications are dropped.                                                                                                                                                             |

Notifications are delivered at least once. The SIM answer and the receipt of a message share its `receipted_message_id`, and differ by the message type of `esm_class`.

### Delivery receipts

A receipt is an SMSC Delivery Receipt (§2.11, §4.6.1, Appendix B):

| Field                                                 | Value                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `source_addr_ton`, `source_addr_npi`, `source_addr`   | The destination of the message, as submitted. |
| `dest_addr_ton`, `dest_addr_npi`, `destination_addr`  | The source of the message, as submitted.      |
| `esm_class`                                           | `0x04`, SMSC Delivery Receipt.                |
| `protocol_id`, `priority_flag`, `registered_delivery` | `0`.                                          |
| `data_coding`                                         | `0x01`, IA5. **Convention**.                  |
| `short_message`                                       | The receipt text.                             |
| `receipted_message_id` (`0x001E`)                     | The `message_id`.                             |
| `message_state` (`0x0427`)                            | See the table below.                          |
| `user_message_reference` (`0x0204`)                   | That of the `submit_sm`, when present.        |

The text follows the example format of Appendix B:

```
id:42 sub:001 dlvrd:001 submit date:2610281430 done date:2610281431 stat:DELIVRD err:000 text:
```

| Field         | Value                                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | The `message_id`, not padded.                                                                                               |
| `sub`         | `001`.                                                                                                                      |
| `dlvrd`       | `001` for a delivered message, else `000`.                                                                                  |
| `submit date` | When the SMSC received the message, `YYMMDDhhmm`, UTC.                                                                      |
| `done date`   | When the message reached its final status, `YYMMDDhhmm`, UTC. For a replaced message, when it was replaced. **Convention**. |
| `stat`, `err` | See the table below.                                                                                                        |
| `text`        | Empty.                                                                                                                      |

| Message status | `stat`    | `message_state` (§5.2.28) | `err`                                                         |
| -------------- | --------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `delivered`    | `DELIVRD` | `2`                       | `000`                                                         |
| `expired`      | `EXPIRED` | `3`                       | `070`, TP-Status `0x46`                                       |
| `replaced`     | `DELETED` | `4`                       | `002`, TP-Status `0x02`                                       |
| `failed`       | `UNDELIV` | `5`                       | The TP-Status of the failure, such as `066`, TP-Status `0x42` |

`err` is the TP-Status (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.15), in decimal. **Convention**. `network_error_code` is not sent.

### SIM answers

The SIM answer is the TP-User-Data of the SMS-DELIVER-REPORT of the last delivery attempt (TS 23.040 §9.2.2.1a), from the RP-ACK, or from the RP-ERROR of an SM delivery failure. For a (U)SIM data download message, it is the SIM's Response Packet (TS 31.115 §4.4; TS 31.111 §7.1.1.1).

It is sent when `registered_delivery` bits 3-2 are `10` or `11`, for any `protocol_id`, as an SME Manual/User Acknowledgement (§2.11). **Convention**.

No SIM answer is sent for a replaced message, or when the SMS-DELIVER-REPORT has no TP-User-Data.

| Field                    | Value                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Addresses                | As in a receipt.                                                                                                                                           |
| `esm_class` message type | `0100`, SME Manual/User Acknowledgement. **Convention**.                                                                                                   |
| `esm_class` UDHI         | `1` when the report has TP-UDHI, or when the message's TP-PID is `0x7F` and the user data starts with a valid user data header (TS 31.115 §4.1). Else `0`. |
| `esm_class`, typical     | `0x50`                                                                                                                                                     |
| `protocol_id`            | The report's TP-PID, else the message's.                                                                                                                   |
| `data_coding`            | See the table below.                                                                                                                                       |
| `short_message`          | The TP-User-Data, its user data header included, such as `027100…`.                                                                                        |
| `receipted_message_id`   | The `message_id`. **Convention**: §5.3.2.12 defines it for receipts.                                                                                       |
| `message_state`          | Absent.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `user_message_reference` | That of the `submit_sm`, when present.                                                                                                                     |

| Report TP-DCS                                 | `data_coding`                                                                      | `short_message`         |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| GSM 7-bit, or no TP-DCS (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.27) | `0x00`                                                                             | Septets, one per octet. |
| UCS2                                          | `0x08`                                                                             | The octets.             |
| 8-bit                                         | That of the `submit_sm` when it is `0x02`, `0x04` or `0xF4` to `0xF7`, else `0x04` | The octets.             |

A SIM that rejects a (U)SIM data download message answers with an RP-ERROR whose TP-Failure-Cause is `0xD5`, (U)SIM data download error. The message fails at once with TP-Status `0x42`: the ESME gets the SIM answer, then the receipt `stat:UNDELIV err:066`.

## `command_status` values

Values the SMSC sends (§5.1.3):

| `command_status`        | Value        | Sent in          | When                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------- | ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ESME_ROK`              | `0x00000000` | Any response     | Success.                                                                                                     |
| `ESME_RINVMSGLEN`       | `0x00000001` | `submit_sm_resp` | `sm_length`, or user data longer than one TPDU.                                                              |
| `ESME_RINVCMDLEN`       | `0x00000002` | `generic_nack`   | `command_length`, or a body of the wrong length.                                                             |
| `ESME_RINVCMDID`        | `0x00000003` | `generic_nack`   | Unsupported or undefined `command_id`.                                                                       |
| `ESME_RINVBNDSTS`       | `0x00000004` | Response         | A request that the session state does not allow.                                                             |
| `ESME_RALYBND`          | `0x00000005` | Bind response    | A bind in a bound state.                                                                                     |
| `ESME_RSYSERR`          | `0x00000008` | `submit_sm_resp` | The message could not be stored or encoded.                                                                  |
| `ESME_RINVSRCADR`       | `0x0000000A` | `submit_sm_resp` | `source_addr`.                                                                                               |
| `ESME_RINVDSTADR`       | `0x0000000B` | `submit_sm_resp` | `destination_addr`.                                                                                          |
| `ESME_RBINDFAIL`        | `0x0000000D` | Bind response    | Any refused bind.                                                                                            |
| `ESME_RINVSUBREP`       | `0x00000042` | `submit_sm_resp` | `replace_if_present_flag` `1`.                                                                               |
| `ESME_RINVESMCLASS`     | `0x00000043` | `submit_sm_resp` | `esm_class`.                                                                                                 |
| `ESME_RSUBMITFAIL`      | `0x00000045` | `submit_sm_resp` | `data_coding`, `protocol_id`, the user data header, or GSM 7-bit, IA5 or UCS2 user data.                     |
| `ESME_RINVSRCTON`       | `0x00000048` | `submit_sm_resp` | `source_addr_ton`.                                                                                           |
| `ESME_RINVSRCNPI`       | `0x00000049` | `submit_sm_resp` | `source_addr_npi`.                                                                                           |
| `ESME_RINVDSTTON`       | `0x00000050` | `submit_sm_resp` | `dest_addr_ton`.                                                                                             |
| `ESME_RINVDSTNPI`       | `0x00000051` | `submit_sm_resp` | `dest_addr_npi`.                                                                                             |
| `ESME_RTHROTTLED`       | `0x00000058` | `submit_sm_resp` | Inbound window full.                                                                                         |
| `ESME_RINVSCHED`        | `0x00000061` | `submit_sm_resp` | `schedule_delivery_time`.                                                                                    |
| `ESME_RINVEXPIRY`       | `0x00000062` | `submit_sm_resp` | `validity_period`.                                                                                           |
| `ESME_RINVDFTMSGID`     | `0x00000063` | `submit_sm_resp` | `sm_default_msg_id`.                                                                                         |
| `ESME_RINVOPTPARSTREAM` | `0x000000C0` | Response         | Optional parameters that do not decode.                                                                      |
| `ESME_ROPTPARNOTALLWD`  | `0x000000C1` | `submit_sm_resp` | `short_message` with `message_payload`; `sar_*` or ports with UDHI.                                          |
| `ESME_RINVPARLEN`       | `0x000000C2` | Response         | A field over its maximum length, or a TLV of the wrong length.                                               |
| `ESME_RINVOPTPARAMVAL`  | `0x000000C4` | `submit_sm_resp` | `sar_*` values; `dest_addr_subunit` against `data_coding`; a TLV that should be a C-Octet String and is not. |
| `ESME_RUNKNOWNERR`      | `0x000000FF` | `generic_nack`   | Invalid `sequence_number`.                                                                                   |

An error response has no body (§4.1.2, §4.1.4, §4.4.2), except `bind_transceiver_resp`, which carries `system_id` (Table 4-6). The SMSC logs the reason of a refused `submit_sm` at level `debug`, with the `system_id`.

Values the SMSC acts on in `deliver_sm_resp`: see [Notifications](#notifications).

## Conventions

Behaviours that SMPP 3.4 does not define:

| Behaviour                                                                                | Where                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TLS from the first octet.                                                                | [Transport](#transport)                                                 |
| A maximum `command_length` of 68 KiB.                                                    | [Transport](#transport)                                                 |
| `data_coding` `0x00` is the GSM 7-bit default alphabet, unpacked.                        | [`data_coding`](#data_coding)                                           |
| `data_coding` `0x02` or `0x04` with `protocol_id` `0x7F` becomes TP-DCS `0xF6`, class 2. | [`data_coding`](#data_coding)                                           |
| A replace type `protocol_id` replaces only messages of the same ESME.                    | [`protocol_id`](#protocol_id)                                           |
| A two-digit year is within 49 years before and 50 years after the current year.          | [Validity and scheduling](#validity-and-scheduling)                     |
| A missing `source_port` or `destination_port` is port 0.                                 | [User data and optional parameters](#user-data-and-optional-parameters) |
| Notifications go to a receiving session of the ESME that submitted the message.          | [Notifications](#notifications)                                         |
| Receipts use `data_coding` `0x01`.                                                       | [Delivery receipts](#delivery-receipts)                                 |
| A replaced message's receipt is `DELETED`, with `done date` the replacement time.        | [Delivery receipts](#delivery-receipts)                                 |
| Receipt `err` is the TP-Status in decimal.                                               | [Delivery receipts](#delivery-receipts)                                 |
| The SIM's answer is an SME Manual/User Acknowledgement, with `receipted_message_id`.     | [SIM answers](#sim-answers)                                             |

## Not supported

- SMPP 3.3 and earlier, and SMPP 5.0.
- `query_sm`, `replace_sm`, `cancel_sm`, `submit_multi`, `data_sm`, `alert_notification` and `outbind`.
- Messages from phones to ESMEs, such as a Response Packet that the SIM sends in an SMS-SUBMIT (TS 31.115 §4.2).
- Splitting user data longer than one TPDU.
- Scheduled delivery, the datagram and transaction modes, SME delivery acknowledgements and intermediate notifications.
- The PROXY protocol.

# System Requirements

Ella SMSC runs on Linux. It supports **amd64** and **arm64** architectures.

|                      | Up to 1,000 subscribers | Up to 100,000 subscribers |
| -------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------- |
| **CPU**              | 1 core                  | 4 cores                   |
| **Memory**           | 1 GB RAM                | 8 GB RAM                  |
| **Disk**             | 10 GB                   | 100 GB                    |
| **Operating System** | Ubuntu 26.04 LTS        | Ubuntu 26.04 LTS          |
| **Kernel**           | SCTP, for Diameter      | SCTP, for Diameter        |

Each column is sized for 20 short messages per subscriber per day, kept for 30 days, with at least 7 times the busiest hour's rate to spare. The 100,000 subscriber host is the one of the [performance reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/performance/index.md).

# API

## Authentication

Requests send a token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

The token is either:

- an access token, from [log in](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/auth/#log-in) or [refresh the access token](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/auth/#refresh-the-access-token), valid for 15 minutes;
- an [API token](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/users/#create-an-api-token), which starts with `ellasmsc_`.

These paths take no token: `GET /api/v1/livez`, `GET /api/v1/readyz`, `GET /api/v1/status`, `GET /api/v1/metrics`, `GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml`, `POST /api/v1/init`, `POST /api/v1/cluster/join`, `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, `/refresh` and `/logout`, and `GET /api/v1/auth/oidc`, `/oidc/login` and `/oidc/callback`.

### Roles

| Role            | `role_id` | Allows                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Admin           | `1`       | Everything.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Read Only       | `2`       | Reading messages without their content, Diameter, operator, delivery and retention settings, ESMEs, and the [cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/cluster/index.md). |
| Network Manager | `3`       | Read Only, plus reading message content, sending messages, updating operator, delivery and retention settings, and managing Diameter peers.                                               |
| Submitter       | `4`       | Sending messages, and reading the messages it sent, their content included.                                                                                                               |

An API token has the role of its user, but cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users, [single sign-on](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/oidc/index.md) or [ESMEs](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md).

Only an Admin manages ESMEs. An [ESME](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md) binds over SMPP with the role of its user.

## Responses

Ella SMSC's API responses are JSON objects. A successful response carries a `result`:

```
{
    "result": "Result content"
}
```

A failed response carries an `error`:

```
{
    "error": "Error message"
}
```

`GET /api/v1/livez` and `GET /api/v1/readyz` answer 204 with no body when they succeed. `GET /api/v1/metrics` returns text in the [Prometheus exposition format](https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats/#text-format-details), `GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml` returns YAML, and unknown paths and methods answer in plain text.

Times are RFC 3339, in UTC.

## OpenAPI Specification

The full API is described by an [OpenAPI 3.1](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0) specification embedded in the binary. Fetch it from any running Ella SMSC instance:

```
GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml
```

## Status codes

- 200 - Success.
- 201 - Created.
- 204 - No content.
- 400 - Bad request.
- 401 - Missing, invalid or expired token.
- 403 - Not allowed for the role or the token.
- 404 - Not found.
- 405 - Method not allowed.
- 409 - Conflict.
- 429 - Too many requests. `Retry-After` is the seconds to wait.
- 500 - Internal server error.
- 502 - The identity provider cannot be reached or used. See [Test an identity provider](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/oidc/#test-an-identity-provider).
- 503 - Not ready. See [Check readiness](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/status/#check-readiness).

# Authentication

## Log In

This path returns an access token, and sets the session cookie, `smsc_session`, or `__Host-smsc_session` over TLS. The session lasts 30 days, and a user has at most 10.

| Method | Path                 |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/login` |

### Request Body

| Field      | Type   | Required | Description                 |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------- |
| `email`    | string | Yes      | Email address, in any case. |
| `password` | string | Yes      | Password.                   |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                              |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401` | Wrong email or password.                                                                                                                 |
| `429` | More than 20 attempts in a minute from the client address, or its IPv6 /64; or more than 100 wrong passwords in an hour for the account. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Login successful",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}
```

## Refresh the Access Token

This path returns a new access token for the session of the cookie.

| Method | Path                   |
| ------ | ---------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/refresh` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                       |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401` | No session, or the session ended. The response clears the cookie. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}
```

## Log Out

This path ends the session of the cookie, and its access tokens, and clears the cookie.

| Method | Path                  |
| ------ | --------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/logout` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                |
| ----- | -------------------------- |
| `204` | Logged out, or no session. |

## Get the Single Sign-On Option

This path tells the login page whether to show the button to sign in through the identity provider.

| Method | Path                |
| ------ | ------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/auth/oidc` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "enabled": true,
        "display_name": "Keycloak"
    }
}
```

## Sign In Through the Identity Provider

The login page sends the browser to this path, which redirects it to the identity provider. It counts toward the login limit of 20 per minute per address.

| Method | Path                      |
| ------ | ------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/auth/oidc/login` |

## Return From the Identity Provider

The identity provider sends the browser back to this path, the redirect URL. Each login completes once. On success, it sets the session cookie, for the [session lifetime](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/oidc/#get-the-oidc-settings), and redirects to `/`. Otherwise, it redirects to `/login?error=<error>`, and the `auth_oidc_login` [audit event](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/observability/#audit-events) gives the details.

| Method | Path                         |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback` |

### Errors

| Error                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rate_limited`       | Too many logins from the address.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `unavailable`        | Single sign-on is off, or the identity provider cannot be reached.                                                                                                                             |
| `failed`             | The login expired, was already used or is invalid, the single sign-on settings changed during it, or the identity provider returned an error.                                                  |
| `denied`             | The user or the identity provider refused access.                                                                                                                                              |
| `not_set_up`         | The identity provider gives no email, or no user has it and no group mapping is set.                                                                                                           |
| `email_not_verified` | The identity provider marks the email as not verified, or does not say and [`trust_unverified_email`](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/oidc/#update-the-oidc-settings) is off. |
| `linked_elsewhere`   | The user with the email is linked to another account at the identity provider.                                                                                                                 |
| `no_group`           | None of the user's groups is mapped to a role.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `groups_overage`     | The user is in too many groups for the identity provider to list them.                                                                                                                         |
| `too_many_users`     | 50 users exist.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `error`              | Internal error.                                                                                                                                                                                |

# Backup

A backup holds every message, user and setting, message content and the single sign-on client secret included. It leaves out the cluster's secrets: the key that signs access tokens, the single sign-on cookie key, and the key and tokens to join a node.

Both paths require Admin. Restoring requires an access token: an API token gets `403`.

## Back Up

This path returns a backup of the database.

| Method | Path             |
| ------ | ---------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/backup` |

### Response

A gzipped tar archive, with `Content-Type: application/gzip` and its file name in `Content-Disposition`, such as `smsc-backup-20261104T120000Z.tar.gz`.

| File            | Description                                         |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `manifest.json` | Format, schema version and time of the backup.      |
| `SHA256SUMS`    | SHA-256 checksums of `smsc.db` and `manifest.json`. |
| `smsc.db`       | The database.                                       |

## Restore

This path replaces every message, user and setting with those of a backup, on every node of a cluster, and closes the SMPP sessions. The cluster keeps its nodes and its secrets.

| Method | Path              |
| ------ | ----------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/restore` |

### Request Body

An archive from [Back Up](#back-up), with `Content-Type: application/gzip`.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Backup restored successfully"
    }
}
```

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                   |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400` | Not a backup, a checksum does not match, or the backup's schema is newer than this version's. |
| `503` | Not ready to restore. Retry.                                                                  |

# Cluster

A cluster is a set of Ella SMSC nodes that share their messages, users and settings. See [High Availability](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/explanation/high_availability/index.md).

Reading the cluster requires Admin, Read Only or Network Manager. The other paths, except [Join a Cluster](#join-a-cluster), require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets `403`.

## Get the Cluster

This path returns the node that answered, its cluster, and every member.

| Method | Path              |
| ------ | ----------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/cluster` |

### Response Fields

| Field                      | Type    | Description                                                                                     |
| -------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `node_id`                  | string  | ID of the node that answered.                                                                   |
| `cluster_id`               | string  | ID of the cluster.                                                                              |
| `clustered`                | boolean | The node has a `cluster` block.                                                                 |
| `leader_id`                | string  | ID of the leader. Absent when there is none.                                                    |
| `term`                     | int     | Election term.                                                                                  |
| `applied_index`            | int     | Last log entry applied by the node.                                                             |
| `commit_index`             | int     | Last log entry committed by the cluster.                                                        |
| `schema`                   | int     | Database schema version of the cluster.                                                         |
| `healthy`                  | boolean | The cluster is healthy. Absent when no leader answers.                                          |
| `failure_tolerance`        | int     | Voters that can fail without stopping writes. Absent when no leader answers.                    |
| `members[].node_id`        | string  | ID of the member.                                                                               |
| `members[].address`        | string  | Cluster address of the member.                                                                  |
| `members[].diameter_label` | string  | First label of the member's Diameter host: `smsc-` and the last 12 hex characters of `node_id`. |
| `members[].display_name`   | string  | Display name of the member. Empty when unset. See [Update a Member](#update-a-member).          |
| `members[].version`        | string  | Version of the member.                                                                          |
| `members[].joined_at`      | string  | Time the member joined.                                                                         |
| `members[].drain_state`    | string  | `active`, `draining` or `drained`. See [Drain a Member](#drain-a-member).                       |
| `members[].suffrage`       | string  | `voter`, `nonvoter` (catching up, or standby), or `none`.                                       |
| `members[].leader`         | boolean | The member is the leader.                                                                       |
| `members[].healthy`        | boolean | The member is healthy. Absent when no leader answers.                                           |
| `members[].last_contact`   | string  | Time since the leader last heard from the member.                                               |
| `members[].applied_index`  | int     | Last log entry applied by the member.                                                           |
| `members[].diverged`       | boolean | The member's database differs from the leader's. Absent when it does not.                       |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "node_id": "0199f6a2-5c1e-7d3a-9b1f-2a4c6e8d0f12",
        "cluster_id": "0199f6a2-4a10-7e55-8c3d-1b2d3e4f5a6b",
        "clustered": true,
        "leader_id": "0199f6a2-5c1e-7d3a-9b1f-2a4c6e8d0f12",
        "term": 4,
        "applied_index": 18342,
        "commit_index": 18342,
        "schema": 1,
        "healthy": true,
        "failure_tolerance": 1,
        "members": [
            {
                "node_id": "0199f6a2-5c1e-7d3a-9b1f-2a4c6e8d0f12",
                "address": "10.0.0.1:7000",
                "diameter_label": "smsc-2a4c6e8d0f12",
                "display_name": "paris-1",
                "version": "v0.9.0",
                "joined_at": "2026-11-05T09:12:44Z",
                "drain_state": "active",
                "suffrage": "voter",
                "leader": true,
                "healthy": true,
                "applied_index": 18342
            },
            {
                "node_id": "0199f6a3-0b77-7c21-a4e0-6f1e2d3c4b5a",
                "address": "10.0.0.2:7000",
                "diameter_label": "smsc-6f1e2d3c4b5a",
                "display_name": "",
                "version": "v0.9.0",
                "joined_at": "2026-11-05T09:14:02Z",
                "drain_state": "active",
                "suffrage": "voter",
                "leader": false,
                "healthy": true,
                "last_contact": "312ms",
                "applied_index": 18342
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Create a Join Token

This path returns a token that lets one node join the cluster, once.

| Method | Path                     |
| ------ | ------------------------ |
| POST   | `/api/v1/cluster/tokens` |

### Request Body

| Field         | Type | Required | Description                                          |
| ------------- | ---- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `ttl_seconds` | int  | No       | Validity of the token, 300 to 86400. Default `1800`. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "token": "AXsiaWQiOiI0ZjJk...",
        "expires_at": "2026-11-05T09:44:02Z"
    }
}
```

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                            |
| ----- | -------------------------------------- |
| `201` | The token.                             |
| `400` | `ttl_seconds` is out of range.         |
| `409` | The node has no `cluster` block.       |
| `410` | The node was removed from the cluster. |

## Join a Cluster

This path joins a node with no user and no message to a cluster. It takes no access token.

| Method | Path                   |
| ------ | ---------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/cluster/join` |

### Request Body

| Field   | Type   | Required | Description                                               |
| ------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `token` | string | Yes      | A token from [Create a Join Token](#create-a-join-token). |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "token": "AXsiaWQiOiI0ZjJk..."
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Joined the cluster"
    }
}
```

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                             |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400` | The token is not valid or expired, or the node runs an older version than the cluster.                                                  |
| `403` | The node has a user.                                                                                                                    |
| `409` | The node has a message, is already in a cluster, or has no `cluster` block, the token was used, or a peer has the node's Diameter host. |
| `429` | Too many attempts from the client address.                                                                                              |
| `502` | No member answered.                                                                                                                     |

## Update a Member

This path sets the display name of a member.

| Method | Path                                |
| ------ | ----------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}` |

### Request Body

| Field          | Type   | Required | Description                      |
| -------------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------- |
| `display_name` | string | Yes      | Up to 63 bytes. Empty clears it. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "display_name": "paris-1"
}
```

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                            |
| ----- | -------------------------------------- |
| `400` | The name is over 63 bytes.             |
| `404` | No such member.                        |
| `410` | The node was removed from the cluster. |

## Drain a Member

| Method | Path                                       |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| POST   | `/api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}/drain`  |
| POST   | `/api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}/resume` |

`drain` sets the member's `drain_state` to `draining`, then `drained`. `resume` sets it to `active`.

| Interface  | Draining or drained member                                                         |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Readiness  | [Fails](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/status/#check-readiness). |
| SMPP       | Closes its sessions and refuses binds.                                             |
| Diameter   | Stays up.                                                                          |
| Leadership | Moves to another voter.                                                            |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                   |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `404` | No such member.                               |
| `409` | The member is the only member of the cluster. |
| `410` | The node was removed from the cluster.        |

## Remove a Member

This path removes a drained member from the cluster. The removed node stops serving.

| Method | Path                                |
| ------ | ----------------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}` |

### Query Parameters

| Name    | Type    | Description                                                                     |
| ------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `force` | boolean | `true` removes a member that is not drained, such as one that is down for good. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                   |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `404` | No such member.                                                               |
| `409` | The member is not drained, or the cluster would lose its majority without it. |
| `503` | No leader. Retry.                                                             |

# Delivery

The delivery settings set how long the SMSC attempts delivery of a message, and when it retries a failed delivery. The [retention](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/retention/index.md) sets how long it keeps a message afterwards.

## Get the Delivery Settings

This path returns the delivery settings.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/delivery` |

### Response Fields

| Field                      | Type  | Description                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default_validity_seconds` | int   | How long delivery of a message without its own validity period is attempted, in seconds. The same applies to status reports. |
| `retry_intervals_seconds`  | array | Wait before each retry, in seconds. The last interval repeats. Empty: a failed delivery is not retried.                      |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "default_validity_seconds": 604800,
        "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300, 900, 3600]
    }
}
```

## Update the Delivery Settings

This path replaces the delivery settings. The new validity applies to the messages received afterwards; the new intervals, to the next retries.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/delivery` |

### Request Body

| Field                      | Type  | Required | Description                    |
| -------------------------- | ----- | -------- | ------------------------------ |
| `default_validity_seconds` | int   | Yes      | `1` to `315360000` (10 years). |
| `retry_intervals_seconds`  | array | Yes      | Each at least 1.               |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "default_validity_seconds": 86400,
    "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300]
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "default_validity_seconds": 86400,
        "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300]
    }
}
```

# Diameter

Configured peers are the Diameter agents that the SMSC connects to, and their routes. Creating, updating and deleting them requires Network Manager or Admin.

## Get the Diameter Status

This path returns the Diameter identity of the SMSC, its peers, and its routes.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/diameter` |

### Response Fields

| Field                  | Type    | Description                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`                 | string  | Origin-Host of the SMSC.                                                                  |
| `realm`                | string  | Origin-Realm of the SMSC.                                                                 |
| `peers`                | array   | Connected and configured peers.                                                           |
| `peers[].id`           | int     | ID of a configured peer.                                                                  |
| `peers[].configured`   | boolean | Whether the peer is configured.                                                           |
| `peers[].host`         | string  | Origin-Host of the peer.                                                                  |
| `peers[].realm`        | string  | Origin-Realm of the peer.                                                                 |
| `peers[].address`      | string  | Remote address of the connection.                                                         |
| `peers[].state`        | string  | `down`, `connecting`, `open`, `suspect`, `reopen` or `closing`.                           |
| `peers[].applications` | array   | Applications the peer supports: `s6c`, `sgd`.                                             |
| `peers[].since`        | string  | Time of the last state change.                                                            |
| `peers[].error`        | string  | Last connection error of a configured peer.                                               |
| `routes`               | array   | The `s6c` route to the HSS, then the routes of the configured peers, default routes last. |
| `routes[].realm`       | string  | Destination-Realm. Empty for a default route.                                             |
| `routes[].default`     | boolean | Whether the route is a default route.                                                     |
| `routes[].application` | string  | `s6c` or `sgd`.                                                                           |
| `routes[].peers`       | array   | Hosts of the open peers of the route.                                                     |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "host": "smsc-013c0a7ca824.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "peers": [
            {
                "configured": false,
                "host": "core.example.org",
                "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "address": "127.0.0.1",
                "state": "open",
                "applications": ["sgd", "s6c"],
                "since": "2026-10-27T18:46:07.330Z"
            },
            {
                "id": 1,
                "configured": true,
                "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                "realm": "ipx.example.net",
                "address": "192.0.2.10",
                "state": "open",
                "applications": ["sgd", "s6c"],
                "since": "2026-10-27T18:47:12.004Z"
            }
        ],
        "routes": [
            {
                "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "default": false,
                "application": "s6c",
                "peers": ["core.example.org"]
            },
            {
                "realm": "",
                "default": true,
                "application": "sgd",
                "peers": ["dea1.ipx.example.net"]
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## List Peers

| Method | Path                     |
| ------ | ------------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/diameter/peers` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 1,
                "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                "addresses": ["192.0.2.10", "198.51.100.10"],
                "port": 3868,
                "routes": [
                    { "default": true, "application": "sgd", "priority": 0 }
                ],
                "status": {
                    "state": "open",
                    "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                    "realm": "ipx.example.net",
                    "since": "2026-10-27T18:47:12.004Z"
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Create a Peer

| Method | Path                     |
| ------ | ------------------------ |
| POST   | `/api/v1/diameter/peers` |

### Request Body

| Field                  | Type    | Required         | Description                                                                                           |
| ---------------------- | ------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`                 | string  | No               | Origin-Host the peer must give. Empty accepts any.                                                    |
| `addresses`            | array   | Yes              | IP addresses of the peer. A peer with a `host` must connect from one of them.                         |
| `port`                 | int     | No               | Default `3868`.                                                                                       |
| `routes`               | array   | No               | Routes of the peer.                                                                                   |
| `routes[].realm`       | string  | Unless `default` | Destination-Realm, e.g. `epc.mnc002.mcc208.3gppnetwork.org`.                                          |
| `routes[].default`     | boolean | No               | Default route: every realm without another route, except the SMSC's own. `sgd` only, without `realm`. |
| `routes[].application` | string  | Yes              | `sgd` or `s6c`. An `s6c` route takes the SMSC's own realm.                                            |
| `routes[].priority`    | int     | No               | Lowest first; equal priorities share the load. Default `0`.                                           |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
    "addresses": ["192.0.2.10", "198.51.100.10"],
    "routes": [
        { "default": true, "application": "sgd" },
        { "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org", "application": "s6c" }
    ]
}
```

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                             |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `201` | The peer, with its `id`.                                                                |
| `400` | Invalid peer.                                                                           |
| `409` | `host` is another peer's or the SMSC's, or two peers without a `host` share an address. |

## Get a Peer

| Method | Path                          |
| ------ | ----------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}` |

### Response Fields

The fields of the request body, plus:

| Field          | Type   | Description                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`           | int    | ID of the peer.                                                                                              |
| `status`       | object | Connection to the peer. Absent until the SMSC applies the peer, and from the responses to create and update. |
| `status.state` | string | `down`, `connecting`, `open`, `suspect`, `reopen` or `closing`.                                              |
| `status.host`  | string | Origin-Host the peer gave.                                                                                   |
| `status.realm` | string | Origin-Realm the peer gave.                                                                                  |
| `status.since` | string | Time of the last state change.                                                                               |
| `status.error` | string | Last connection error.                                                                                       |

## Update a Peer

The request body is that of [Create a Peer](#create-a-peer). A change of `host`, `addresses` or `port` reconnects.

| Method | Path                          |
| ------ | ----------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}` |

## Delete a Peer

| Method | Path                          |
| ------ | ----------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}` |

# ESMEs

An ESME account is what an External Short Message Entity, such as an OTA platform, binds to the [SMPP listener](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md) with, with at most 4 sessions at once. It acts as its user: the messages it submits are the user's, and the user's role decides which binds it may make. See [Binds](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/#binds).

Reading ESMEs requires Admin, Read Only or Network Manager. Creating, updating and deleting them requires Admin, and an access token: an API token gets `403`.

## List ESMEs

| Method | Path            |
| ------ | --------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/esmes` |

### Response Fields

| Field                       | Type   | Description                                 |
| --------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `system_id`                 | string | The `system_id` the ESME binds with.        |
| `user`                      | string | Email of the user the ESME acts as.         |
| `allowed_networks`          | array  | IP prefixes the ESME may bind from.         |
| `created_at`                | string | Time the ESME was created.                  |
| `sessions`                  | array  | Bound sessions, oldest first.               |
| `sessions[].bind_type`      | string | `transmitter`, `receiver` or `transceiver`. |
| `sessions[].remote_address` | string | Address and port of the client.             |
| `sessions[].bound_at`       | string | Time of the bind.                           |

The password is never returned.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "system_id": "ota",
                "user": "ota@example.com",
                "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"],
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:40:02.118Z",
                "sessions": [
                    {
                        "bind_type": "transceiver",
                        "remote_address": "10.1.0.5:40312",
                        "bound_at": "2026-10-27T18:41:55.906Z"
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Create an ESME

At most 50 ESMEs. Without a `password`, the SMSC generates one of 8 letters and digits, and returns it as `password` in this response only.

| Method | Path            |
| ------ | --------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/esmes` |

### Request Body

| Field              | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `system_id`        | string | Yes      | 1 to 15 printable ASCII characters (SMPP 3.4 §4.1.1).                                                      |
| `user`             | string | Yes      | Email of an existing user, the user the ESME acts as.                                                      |
| `password`         | string | No       | 1 to 8 printable ASCII characters (SMPP 3.4 §4.1.1). Default: generated.                                   |
| `allowed_networks` | array  | No       | IP prefixes, such as `10.1.0.0/24` or `2001:db8::/64`, at most 50. Default: none, which allows no address. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "system_id": "ota",
    "user": "ota@example.com",
    "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"]
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "system_id": "ota",
        "user": "ota@example.com",
        "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"],
        "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:40:02.118Z",
        "sessions": [],
        "password": "q7Rk2LxW"
    }
}
```

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                  |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `201` | The ESME, with the generated `password` when none was given. |
| `400` | Invalid field, no user with the email, or 50 ESMEs exist.    |
| `409` | An ESME has the `system_id`.                                 |

## Get an ESME

| Method | Path                        |
| ------ | --------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/esmes/{system_id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name        | Type   | Description                               |
| ----------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `system_id` | string | The `system_id` of the ESME, URL-encoded. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                   |
| ----- | ----------------------------- |
| `404` | No ESME has this `system_id`. |

## Update an ESME

This path replaces the allowed networks of an ESME, and its password when one is given, and closes its sessions, which bind again under the new settings. The `system_id` and the user cannot be changed.

| Method | Path                        |
| ------ | --------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/esmes/{system_id}` |

### Request Body

| Field              | Type   | Required | Description                                                        |
| ------------------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `password`         | string | No       | 1 to 8 printable ASCII characters. Without it, the password stays. |
| `allowed_networks` | array  | Yes      | As in [Create an ESME](#create-an-esme).                           |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                   |
| ----- | ----------------------------- |
| `200` | The ESME.                     |
| `400` | Invalid field.                |
| `404` | No ESME has this `system_id`. |

## Delete an ESME

This path deletes an ESME, closes its sessions, and drops the receipts and SIM answers not yet sent to it. Its messages stay, as its user's. Deleting the user deletes its ESMEs.
