| Method | Path                        |
| ------ | --------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/esmes/{system_id}` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "ESME deleted successfully"
    }
}
```

# Initialize

## Initialize Ella SMSC

This path creates the first user, an Admin, and logs it in.

| Method | Path           |
| ------ | -------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/init` |

### Request Body

| Field      | Type   | Required | Description    |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | -------------- |
| `email`    | string | Yes      | Email address. |
| `password` | string | Yes      | 8 to 72 bytes. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `201` | Created.                                   |
| `403` | A user exists.                             |
| `429` | Too many attempts from the client address. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "password": "correct horse"
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "System initialized successfully",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}
```

# Messages

A message is a short message the SMSC received, from a phone, from the API, or from an ESME over [SMPP](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md), with its delivery status and the status reports the SMSC returned to the phone that sent it. A text longer than one short message is split into parts, one message each.

Responses carry no content. [Get the content of a message](#get-the-content-of-a-message) returns it, and logs an audit event.

## Create a Message

This path submits a text message, or a binary message, to a phone. It returns one message per part.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| POST   | `/api/v1/messages` |

### Request Body

| Field                        | Type   | Required                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ------ | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `from`                       | string | Yes                        | Shown to the recipient as the sender. An E.164 number with `+`, or a name of 1 to 11 ASCII letters and digits, with single spaces between words, that is not all digits, such as `EllaSMSC`. A value without `+` is a name, delivered as given.                                                                                                                                        |
| `to`                         | string | Yes                        | E.164 number with `+` of the recipient.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `text`                       | string | One of `text` and `binary` | Not empty. GSM-7 if every character is in the GSM 7-bit default alphabet or its extension table, else UCS-2. Up to 255 parts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `binary`                     | object | One of `text` and `binary` | TPDU parameters of one short message, delivered unchanged.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `binary.protocol_identifier` | int    | No                         | TP-PID (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.9), `0` to `255`. Default `0`. Not `32` to `62`, telematic interworking. `65` to `71`, replace types 1 to 7, replace the pending message of the same type from the same `from`, submitted by the same user; never a message from a phone or an ESME. `72`, device triggering, needs an application port addressing information element in `user_data_header`. |
| `binary.data_coding_scheme`  | int    | Yes                        | TP-DCS (TS 23.038 §4), `0` to `255`. Not a GSM 7-bit, UCS2 or reserved coding. Message class 2 when `protocol_identifier` is `124`, ANSI-136 R-DATA, or `127`, (U)SIM data download.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `binary.user_data_header`    | string | No                         | TP-UDH (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24) in hexadecimal, its length octet included.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `binary.user_data`           | string | Yes                        | TP-UD after the header, in hexadecimal. May be empty. At most 140 octets with `user_data_header`. Not split into parts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `validity_seconds`           | int    | No                         | How long delivery is attempted, `1` to `315360000` (10 years). Default: the default validity of the [delivery settings](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/delivery/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                           |

A message from the API never asks for status reports.

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `400` | A field is missing or invalid, both or neither of `text` and `binary`, the text needs more than 255 parts, or the binary user data is over 140 octets. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "from": "+15550001000",
    "to": "+15551230002",
    "text": "Your code is 1234"
}
```

### Sample Request (Binary)

```
{
    "from": "+15550001000",
    "to": "+15551230002",
    "binary": {
        "protocol_identifier": 127,
        "data_coding_scheme": 246,
        "user_data_header": "027000",
        "user_data": "0011223344"
    }
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 1,
                "from": "+15550001000",
                "to": "+15551230002",
                "encoding": "gsm7",
                "status": "pending",
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:44:19.436Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-10-27T18:44:19.436Z",
                "expires_at": "2026-11-03T18:44:19.436Z",
                "next_attempt_at": "2026-10-27T18:44:19.436Z",
                "status_report": {
                    "requested": false,
                    "reports": []
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## List Messages

This path returns the list of messages, most recent first. For a Submitter, only the messages it sent.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/messages` |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed                                                                                      | Description                                                                                                          |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `to`       | query | str  |         | 1 to 15 digits, after an optional `+`                                                        | Recipient: the numbers that contain these digits. `+1555123` and `1555123` match `+15551230002`, and so does `0002`. |
| `from`     | query | str  |         | 1 to 15 digits, after an optional `+`, or a name as in [Create a Message](#create-a-message) | Sender: the numbers that contain these digits, or the name, in any case.                                             |
| `status`   | query | str  |         | `pending`, `delivered`, `failed`, `expired`, `replaced`                                      | Status.                                                                                                              |
| `start`    | query | str  |         | RFC 3339 time                                                                                | Created at or after.                                                                                                 |
| `end`      | query | str  |         | RFC 3339 time, not before `start`                                                            | Created before.                                                                                                      |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`                                                                                       | 1-based page index.                                                                                                  |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100`                                                                                      | Number of items per page.                                                                                            |

### Response Fields

| Field                                     | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`                                      | int     | Message identifier.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `from`                                    | string  | Sender: the MSISDN of the phone, an E.164 number with `+`, the `from` of the API request, or the `source_addr` of the `submit_sm`, with `+` when international.                      |
| `to`                                      | string  | Recipient, an E.164 number with `+`.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `encoding`                                | string  | `gsm7`, `ucs2` or `binary`.                                                                                                                                                          |
| `concatenation`                           | object  | Present for a part of a longer message.                                                                                                                                              |
| `concatenation.reference`                 | int     | Reference shared by the parts of the message.                                                                                                                                        |
| `concatenation.part`                      | int     | Number of this part, from 1.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `concatenation.total`                     | int     | Number of parts.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `status`                                  | string  | See [Statuses](#statuses).                                                                                                                                                           |
| `created_at`                              | string  | Time the SMSC received the message.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `updated_at`                              | string  | Time of the last change.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `expires_at`                              | string  | End of the validity period.                                                                                                                                                          |
| `next_attempt_at`                         | string  | Time of the next delivery attempt. Present while `pending`.                                                                                                                          |
| `status_report`                           | object  | Status reports on the message.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `status_report.requested`                 | boolean | Whether the phone that sent the message asked for status reports.                                                                                                                    |
| `status_report.reports`                   | array   | Status reports the SMSC returned to that phone, oldest first.                                                                                                                        |
| `status_report.reports[].id`              | int     | Status report identifier.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `status_report.reports[].tp_status`       | int     | TP-Status the report gives (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.15).                                                                                                                                    |
| `status_report.reports[].tp_status_name`  | string  | Meaning of `tp_status`, e.g. `received`, `replaced`, `no_response`, `validity_period_expired`.                                                                                       |
| `status_report.reports[].status`          | string  | Delivery of the report to the phone: `pending`, `delivered`, `failed` or `expired`.                                                                                                  |
| `status_report.reports[].created_at`      | string  | Time the SMSC made the report.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `status_report.reports[].updated_at`      | string  | Time of the last change.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `status_report.reports[].expires_at`      | string  | End of the report's validity period.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `status_report.reports[].next_attempt_at` | string  | Time of the next delivery attempt of the report. Present while `pending`.                                                                                                            |
| `submitted_by`                            | string  | Email of the user that sent the message over the API, or of the user of the ESME that sent it over SMPP. Absent for a message from a phone.                                          |
| `system_id`                               | string  | `system_id` of the [ESME](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md) that sent the message over SMPP. Absent for other messages, and once the ESME is deleted. |

### Statuses

| Status      | When                                                                                                                             |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pending`   | Not yet delivered, within its validity period.                                                                                   |
| `delivered` | A serving node took it.                                                                                                          |
| `failed`    | The recipient is unknown, is not allowed SMS, or has no serving node that supports SGd.                                          |
| `failed`    | The network rejected the recipient's subscription or phone as illegal.                                                           |
| `failed`    | The SIM refused a (U)SIM data download message.                                                                                  |
| `failed`    | An attempt failed, and the message is single-shot or retries are off.                                                            |
| `expired`   | Its validity period ended before its delivery.                                                                                   |
| `replaced`  | A later message of the same replace type, from the same sender and submitter, before its delivery: the same phone, user or ESME. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 4,
                "from": "+15550001000",
                "to": "+15551230001",
                "encoding": "gsm7",
                "concatenation": {
                    "reference": 74,
                    "part": 2,
                    "total": 2
                },
                "status": "pending",
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:53:37.120Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-10-27T18:54:07.151Z",
                "expires_at": "2026-11-03T18:53:37.120Z",
                "next_attempt_at": "2026-10-27T18:55:07.151Z",
                "status_report": {
                    "requested": false,
                    "reports": []
                }
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 1,
        "total_count": 3
    }
}
```

## Count Messages

This path returns the number of messages in each status. For a Submitter, only the messages it sent.

| Method | Path                      |
| ------ | ------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/messages/counts` |

### Query Parameters

| Name    | In    | Type | Default | Allowed                           | Description          |
| ------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| `start` | query | str  |         | RFC 3339 time                     | Created at or after. |
| `end`   | query | str  |         | RFC 3339 time, not before `start` | Created before.      |

### Response Fields

| Field       | Type | Description                                    |
| ----------- | ---- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `pending`   | int  | Messages `pending`. See [Statuses](#statuses). |
| `delivered` | int  | Messages `delivered`.                          |
| `failed`    | int  | Messages `failed`.                             |
| `expired`   | int  | Messages `expired`.                            |
| `replaced`  | int  | Messages `replaced`.                           |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "pending": 11,
        "delivered": 105,
        "failed": 6,
        "expired": 4,
        "replaced": 0
    }
}
```

## Get a Message

This path returns a specific message. For a Submitter, a message it did not send is not found.

| Method | Path                    |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/messages/{id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type | Description         |
| ---- | ---- | ------------------- |
| `id` | int  | Message identifier. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                     |
| ----- | ------------------------------- |
| `404` | No message has this identifier. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "id": 1,
        "from": "+15551230001",
        "to": "+15551230002",
        "encoding": "gsm7",
        "status": "delivered",
        "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:07.350Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.355Z",
        "expires_at": "2026-11-03T18:46:07.350Z",
        "status_report": {
            "requested": true,
            "reports": [
                {
                    "id": 2,
                    "tp_status": 0,
                    "tp_status_name": "received",
                    "status": "delivered",
                    "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.355Z",
                    "updated_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.356Z",
                    "expires_at": "2026-11-03T18:46:10.355Z"
                }
            ]
        }
    }
}
```

## Get the Content of a Message

This path returns the content of a message, and logs an audit event `read_message_content` with the email of the caller. For a Submitter, a message it did not send is not found. A Read Only user cannot read content.

| Method | Path                            |
| ------ | ------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/messages/{id}/content` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type | Description         |
| ---- | ---- | ------------------- |
| `id` | int  | Message identifier. |

### Response Fields

| Field                                   | Type   | Description                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`                                  | string | Text of the part. Absent for a binary message.                                                                                  |
| `binary`                                | object | TPDU parameters of a binary message.                                                                                            |
| `binary.protocol_identifier`            | int    | TP-PID.                                                                                                                         |
| `binary.data_coding_scheme`             | int    | TP-DCS.                                                                                                                         |
| `binary.user_data_header`               | string | TP-UDH in hexadecimal, its length octet included. Absent when there is none.                                                    |
| `binary.user_data`                      | string | TP-UD after the header, in hexadecimal.                                                                                         |
| `deliver_reports`                       | array  | SMS-DELIVER-REPORTs (TS 23.040 §9.2.2.1a) the serving nodes passed on, oldest first. Absent when there are none.                |
| `deliver_reports[].attempt_id`          | int    | [Delivery attempt](#list-delivery-attempts) of the report: in the RP-ACK when its `outcome` is `success`, else in the RP-ERROR. |
| `deliver_reports[].tpdu`                | string | The report in hexadecimal. The other `deliver_reports[]` fields are absent when it does not decode.                             |
| `deliver_reports[].protocol_identifier` | int    | TP-PID, when present.                                                                                                           |
| `deliver_reports[].data_coding_scheme`  | int    | TP-DCS, when present.                                                                                                           |
| `deliver_reports[].user_data_header`    | string | TP-UDH in hexadecimal, when present.                                                                                            |
| `deliver_reports[].user_data`           | string | TP-UD after the header, in hexadecimal, when present.                                                                           |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                     |
| ----- | ------------------------------- |
| `404` | No message has this identifier. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "text": "Your code is 1234"
    }
}
```

### Sample Response (Binary)

```
{
    "result": {
        "binary": {
            "protocol_identifier": 127,
            "data_coding_scheme": 246,
            "user_data_header": "027000",
            "user_data": "0011223344"
        },
        "deliver_reports": [
            {
                "attempt_id": 2,
                "tpdu": "00077ff602cafe",
                "protocol_identifier": 127,
                "data_coding_scheme": 246,
                "user_data": "cafe"
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## List Delivery Attempts

This path returns the routing and delivery attempts of a message, oldest first. For a Submitter, a message it did not send is not found.

| Method | Path                             |
| ------ | -------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/messages/{id}/attempts` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type | Description         |
| ---- | ---- | ------------------- |
| `id` | int  | Message identifier. |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed | Description               |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | ------- | ------------------------- |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`  | 1-based page index.       |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100` | Number of items per page. |

### Response Fields

| Field                     | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                      | int    | Attempt identifier.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `started_at`              | string | Start of the attempt.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `completed_at`            | string | End of the attempt.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `step`                    | string | `routing`: a routing lookup at the HSS, over S6c. `delivery`: a delivery to a serving node, over SGd.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `node`                    | string | Host of the HSS that answered the routing lookup, or of the serving node.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `node_type`               | string | Type of the serving node: `mme`, `sgsn`, `ip_sm_gw`, `smsf_3gpp` or `smsf_non_3gpp`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `outcome`                 | string | `success`; `no_hss`, no HSS connected; `unreachable`, the serving node not connected; `timeout`, no answer in time; the error the node gave: `user_unknown`, `absent_user`, `user_busy_for_mt_sms`, `facility_not_supported`, `illegal_user`, `illegal_equipment`, `sm_delivery_failure`, `service_not_subscribed`, `service_barred`, `mwd_list_full`; `diameter_error`, another error answer; or `error`. |
| `result_code`             | int    | Result-Code or Experimental-Result-Code of the answer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `vendor_id`               | int    | Vendor-Id of an Experimental-Result-Code.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `failure_cause`           | string | SM-Delivery-Failure-Cause of an `sm_delivery_failure`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `tp_failure_cause`        | string | TP-Failure-Cause the phone gave.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `absent_user_diagnostics` | object | Why the phone is unreachable, by node: `mme`, `msc`, `sgsn`, `ip_sm_gw`, `smsf_3gpp`, `smsf_non_3gpp`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

A value the SMSC did not observe is absent.

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                     |
| ----- | ------------------------------- |
| `404` | No message has this identifier. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 1,
                "started_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:07.351Z",
                "completed_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:07.351Z",
                "step": "routing",
                "node": "core.example.org",
                "outcome": "absent_user",
                "result_code": 5550,
                "vendor_id": 10415,
                "absent_user_diagnostics": {
                    "mme": "imsi_detached"
                }
            },
            {
                "id": 2,
                "started_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.354Z",
                "completed_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.355Z",
                "step": "routing",
                "node": "core.example.org",
                "outcome": "success",
                "result_code": 2001
            },
            {
                "id": 3,
                "started_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.355Z",
                "completed_at": "2026-10-27T18:46:10.355Z",
                "step": "delivery",
                "node": "core.example.org",
                "node_type": "mme",
                "outcome": "success",
                "result_code": 2001
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 3
    }
}
```

# Metrics

## Get Metrics

This path returns the metrics of the SMSC in the [Prometheus exposition format](https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats/#text-format-details), negotiated from the request's `Accept` header. See [Observability](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/observability/#metrics) for the list.

| Method | Path              |
| ------ | ----------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/metrics` |

### Sample Response

```
# HELP ellasmsc_hss_peers Open Diameter peers in the operator's realm that serve S6c, which the SMSC asks to route messages. At 0, messages to phones wait.
# TYPE ellasmsc_hss_peers gauge
ellasmsc_hss_peers 0
# HELP ellasmsc_messages_pending Short messages and status reports waiting for delivery, by type (message, status_report) and state: due (to be delivered now, or being delivered) or waiting (for a retry or for the phone to be reachable). Due messages that stay due mean the deliverer is falling behind.
# TYPE ellasmsc_messages_pending gauge
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="due",type="message"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="due",type="status_report"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="waiting",type="message"} 2
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="waiting",type="status_report"} 0
# HELP ellasmsc_messages_received_total Short messages received, one per TPDU, by origin (mobile, api) and result (accepted, rejected, error).
# TYPE ellasmsc_messages_received_total counter
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="api",result="accepted"} 2
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="api",result="error"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="accepted"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="error"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="rejected"} 0
```

# Single Sign-On

These paths configure sign-in to the UI through an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider. They require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets `403`.

## Get the OIDC Settings

This path never returns the client secret.

| Method | Path           |
| ------ | -------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/oidc` |

### Response Fields

| Field                      | Type    | Description                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`                  | boolean | Users can sign in through the identity provider.                                                                                          |
| `external_url`             | string  | The URL users reach Ella SMSC at.                                                                                                         |
| `redirect_url`             | string  | The redirect URL to register at the identity provider. Empty without an external URL.                                                     |
| `issuer`                   | string  | The identity provider's issuer URL.                                                                                                       |
| `client_id`                | string  | The client ID registered at the identity provider.                                                                                        |
| `client_secret_set`        | boolean | A client secret is stored.                                                                                                                |
| `display_name`             | string  | The name on the login button.                                                                                                             |
| `scopes`                   | array   | The scopes requested. Initially `openid`, `email` and `profile`.                                                                          |
| `session_lifetime_seconds` | int     | How long a session started through the identity provider lasts. Initially `86400`.                                                        |
| `trust_unverified_email`   | boolean | Email addresses are accepted when the identity provider does not send `email_verified`. An `email_verified` of `false` is always refused. |
| `ca_certificate`           | string  | PEM certificates the identity provider's TLS certificate must chain to. Empty: the system's.                                              |
| `groups_claim`             | string  | The claim, in the ID token or UserInfo, that holds the user's groups.                                                                     |
| `group_roles`              | array   | Group-to-role mappings, in order.                                                                                                         |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "enabled": true,
        "external_url": "https://smsc.example.com",
        "redirect_url": "https://smsc.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback",
        "issuer": "https://idp.example.com/realms/smsc",
        "client_id": "smsc",
        "client_secret_set": true,
        "display_name": "Keycloak",
        "scopes": ["openid", "email", "profile"],
        "session_lifetime_seconds": 86400,
        "trust_unverified_email": false,
        "ca_certificate": "",
        "groups_claim": "groups",
        "group_roles": [
            {"group": "smsc-admins", "role_id": 1},
            {"group": "noc", "role_id": 3}
        ]
    }
}
```

## Update the OIDC Settings

This path replaces the settings, which take effect at once. Disabling OIDC or changing the issuer ends all sessions started through the identity provider.

| Method | Path           |
| ------ | -------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/oidc` |

### Request Body

| Field                      | Type    | Required                                                                 | Description                                                                                                |
| -------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`                  | boolean | Yes                                                                      |                                                                                                            |
| `external_url`             | string  | When enabled                                                             | An https URL with no path. Stored as `https://host[:port]`.                                                |
| `issuer`                   | string  | When enabled                                                             | An https URL with no query or fragment, as the identity provider gives it.                                 |
| `client_id`                | string  | When enabled                                                             | At most 255 characters.                                                                                    |
| `client_secret`            | string  | When enabled and none is stored, or when `issuer` or `client_id` changes | At most 255 characters. Empty or absent: the stored secret is kept.                                        |
| `display_name`             | string  | When enabled                                                             | At most 64 characters.                                                                                     |
| `scopes`                   | array   | Yes                                                                      | At most 20, including `openid` and `email`.                                                                |
| `session_lifetime_seconds` | int     | Yes                                                                      | `300` to `2592000` (30 days).                                                                              |
| `trust_unverified_email`   | boolean | No                                                                       | Default `false`.                                                                                           |
| `ca_certificate`           | string  | No                                                                       | PEM certificates.                                                                                          |
| `groups_claim`             | string  | With `group_roles`                                                       | The claim name, such as `groups`.                                                                          |
| `group_roles`              | array   | No                                                                       | At most 100 objects with a `group`, matched exactly, and a `role_id`, `1` to `4`. Each group at most once. |

### Group Roles

| `group_roles` | At each login through the identity provider                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Empty         | An Admin sets the role. Someone with no user in Ella SMSC is refused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Not empty     | The first mapping whose group the user is in sets the role. A user in none is refused. Someone with no user in Ella SMSC gets one, with that role. A [pinned](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/users/#update-a-user) role is kept, whatever the groups. The last Admin with a password stays Admin. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                  |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `200` | Updated. The response holds the new settings.                                |
| `400` | Invalid field, or `issuer` or `client_id` changes without a `client_secret`. |

## Test an Identity Provider

This path checks that Ella SMSC can use an identity provider. It changes no setting.

| Method | Path                     |
| ------ | ------------------------ |
| POST   | `/api/v1/oidc/discovery` |

### Request Body

| Field            | Type   | Required | Description                                 |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `issuer`         | string | Yes      | The issuer URL to test.                     |
| `ca_certificate` | string | No       | PEM certificates to trust for the provider. |

### Response Fields

| Field                        | Type    | Description                                                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `issuer`                     | string  | The provider's issuer.                                                                |
| `authorization_endpoint`     | string  |                                                                                       |
| `token_endpoint`             | string  |                                                                                       |
| `token_endpoint_auth_method` | string  | `client_secret_basic` or `client_secret_post`: how Ella SMSC sends the client secret. |
| `userinfo_endpoint`          | string  | Empty if the provider has none.                                                       |
| `jwks_uri`                   | string  |                                                                                       |
| `signing_algorithms`         | array   | The algorithms the provider signs ID tokens with.                                     |
| `keys`                       | int     | The number of signing keys.                                                           |
| `pkce`                       | boolean | The provider supports PKCE.                                                           |
| `issuer_parameter`           | boolean | The provider supports RFC 9207.                                                       |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `200` | The provider can be used.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `400` | Invalid issuer or CA certificate.                                                                                                                                             |
| `502` | The provider cannot be reached or cannot be used, for example because its token endpoint supports neither `client_secret_basic` nor `client_secret_post`. The error says why. |

# Operator

The operator is the PLMN of the SMSC, from which its Diameter identity derives, its service centre address, and the numbering plan that converts the numbers phones send to E.164 numbers.

## Get the Operator

This path returns the operator settings.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/operator` |

### Response Fields

| Field                            | Type   | Description                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mcc`                            | string | Mobile Country Code.                                                                                       |
| `mnc`                            | string | Mobile Network Code.                                                                                       |
| `service_centre_address`         | string | E.164 number of the SMSC, which phones have as SMSC number.                                                |
| `numbering`                      | object | Conversion of the numbers phones send to E.164 numbers.                                                    |
| `numbering.country_code`         | string | Country code, added to the numbers phones send in national format.                                         |
| `numbering.national_prefix`      | string | Prefix that phones dial before a national number, removed before the country code is added. Empty if none. |
| `numbering.international_prefix` | string | Prefix that phones dial before an international number, removed. Empty if none.                            |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011"
        }
    }
}
```

## Update the Operator

This path replaces the operator settings. A change of MCC or MNC changes the Diameter host and realm: the SMSC restarts Diameter, and its peers reconnect.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/operator` |

### Request Body

| Field                            | Type   | Required | Description                                                       |
| -------------------------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mcc`                            | string | Yes      | 3 digits.                                                         |
| `mnc`                            | string | Yes      | 2 or 3 digits.                                                    |
| `service_centre_address`         | string | Yes      | E.164 number with `+`, e.g. `+15550000000`.                       |
| `numbering`                      | object | Yes      |                                                                   |
| `numbering.country_code`         | string | Yes      | 1 to 3 digits, not starting with 0.                               |
| `numbering.national_prefix`      | string | Yes      | Up to 4 digits. Differs from `international_prefix` unless empty. |
| `numbering.international_prefix` | string | Yes      | Up to 4 digits.                                                   |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "mcc": "001",
    "mnc": "01",
    "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
    "numbering": {
        "country_code": "1",
        "national_prefix": "1",
        "international_prefix": "011"
    }
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011"
        }
    }
}
```

# Pprof

These paths serve the [net/http/pprof](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http/pprof) API. They require Admin, and accept an API token.

## Profiling Endpoints

| Method    | Path                          | Description                                              |
| --------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/`              | An HTML page listing the available profiles.             |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/allocs`        | A sampling of all past memory allocations.               |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/cmdline`       | The command line invocation of the program.              |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/goroutine`     | Stack traces of all current goroutines.                  |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/goroutineleak` | Stack traces of all leaked goroutines.                   |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/heap`          | A sampling of memory allocations of live objects.        |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/profile`       | A CPU profile, of 30 seconds by default.                 |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/threadcreate`  | Stack traces that led to the creation of new OS threads. |
| GET       | `/api/v1/pprof/trace`         | An execution trace, of 1 second by default.              |
| GET, POST | `/api/v1/pprof/symbol`        | Function names of program counters.                      |

### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Paths                                         | Description                                                                         |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seconds` | `profile`, `trace`                            | Duration of the capture.                                                            |
| `seconds` | `allocs`, `goroutine`, `heap`                 | Returns the difference of the profile over this duration.                           |
| `debug`   | `allocs`, `goroutine`, `heap`, `threadcreate` | `0`: protobuf. `1`: text. `2` (`goroutine`): stack traces in the format of a panic. |
| `gc`      | `heap`                                        | `1`: runs a garbage collection first.                                               |

# Retention

The retention sets how long the SMSC keeps a message once it has its final status: `delivered`, `failed`, `expired` or `replaced`. The SMSC then deletes it, with its status reports and delivery attempts, within the hour. It keeps a message until its status reports, too, have had their final status for that long.

## Get the Retention

This path returns the retention.

| Method | Path                         |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/messages/retention` |

### Response Fields

| Field  | Type | Description                                                         |
| ------ | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `days` | int  | Days a message is kept once it has its final status. Default: `30`. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "days": 30
    }
}
```

## Update the Retention

This path replaces the retention. It applies from the next deletion, within the hour.

| Method | Path                         |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/messages/retention` |

### Request Body

| Field  | Type | Required | Description |
| ------ | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `days` | int  | Yes      | At least 1. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "days": 7
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "days": 7
    }
}
```

| `clustered`      | boolean | Whether the configuration file has a `cluster` block.                                                                                         |
| `node_id`        | string  | ID of the node that answered.                                                                                                                 |

This path returns whether the SMSC can serve requests: its database answers, it is not shutting down, and, in a cluster, it is not draining and is in contact with the leader.

# Users

Paths under `/api/v1/users/me` act on the user of the token. The others require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets `403`.

## Get My User

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/users/me` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "email": "admin@example.com",
        "role_id": 1,
        "role_pinned": false,
        "password_set": true,
        "oidc_linked": false
    }
}
```

### Response Fields

| Field          | Type    | Description                                                                                                                          |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `email`        | string  | Email address.                                                                                                                       |
| `role_id`      | int     | `1` to `4`. See [roles](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/#roles).                                                    |
| `role_pinned`  | boolean | The role is kept whatever the user's [groups](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/oidc/#group-roles).                   |
| `password_set` | boolean | The user has a password.                                                                                                             |
| `oidc_linked`  | boolean | The user is linked to an account at the current [identity provider](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/oidc/index.md). |

The other paths that return users return the same fields.

## Update My Password

This path ends the user's other sessions. It requires an access token.

| Method | Path                        |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                       |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400` | Wrong current password, or invalid new password.                                  |
| `409` | The user has no password.                                                         |

## Create a User

At most 50 users.

| `role_id`     | int     | Yes      | `1` to `4`. See [roles](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/#roles).                                                                  |
| `role_pinned` | boolean | No       | Keep the role whatever the user's [groups](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/oidc/#group-roles). Default `false`.                   |

| Code  | Description                        |

## Update a User

This path sets the role of a user. A role change ends the user's sessions and the SMPP sessions of its [ESMEs](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md). An Admin cannot change its own role, and the last Admin with a password stays an Admin.

| Method | Path                    |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/users/{email}` |

### Request Body

| Field         | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `role_id`     | int     | Yes      | `1` to `4`.                                                                                                                                            |
| `role_pinned` | boolean | No       | Keep the role whatever the user's [groups](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/oidc/#group-roles). Without it, the current value is kept. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `409` | The role comes from the user's [groups](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/oidc/#group-roles) and `role_pinned` is not `true`, or the user is the last Admin with a password. |

## Update a User's Password

This path ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot update its own password here.

| Method | Path                             |
| ------ | -------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/users/{email}/password` |

### Request Body

| Field      | Type   | Required | Description    |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | -------------- |
| `password` | string | Yes      | 8 to 72 bytes. |

## Remove a User's Password

This path removes the password of a user, who can then sign in only through the [identity provider](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/oidc/index.md). It ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot remove its own password, and the last Admin with a password keeps it.

| Method | Path                             |
| ------ | -------------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}/password` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                     |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `409` | The user has no password, or is the last Admin with a password. |

## Unlink a User

This path unlinks a user from their account at the identity provider, and ends the sessions started through it. Their next login through the identity provider links them again by email. An Admin cannot unlink itself.

| Method | Path                         |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}/oidc` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                        |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `404` | No user has the email, or the user is not linked to the current identity provider. |

## Delete a User

This path deletes the user with its sessions, API tokens and [ESMEs](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/esmes/index.md). An Admin cannot delete itself, and the last Admin with a password cannot be deleted.

| Method | Path                    |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                 |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `409` | The user is the last Admin with a password. |

# Explanation

# Explanation

These explanations provide context on how Ella SMSC works.

- [Architecture](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/explanation/architecture/index.md)
- [Security](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/explanation/security/index.md)
- [Single sign-on](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/explanation/single_sign_on/index.md)
- [High availability](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/explanation/high_availability/index.md)

# Architecture

Ella SMSC is a Short Message Service Centre (SMSC) for private 4G and 5G networks. It stores the short messages sent to the network's subscribers, and delivers them when their phones can receive them.

Ella SMSC is a single application, with an embedded database, an embedded web UI, and an HTTP API.

## How phones send and receive SMS

A phone exchanges SMS with Ella SMSC in one of two ways: over NAS, through the core network, or over IP, through the IMS.

### SMS over NAS

SMS over NAS

With SMS over NAS, the message travels inside the signalling the phone already exchanges with the core network to attach and stay registered. It needs no IMS.

### SMS over IP

SMS over IP

With SMS over IP, the phone sends and receives its messages as SIP messages through the IMS. An IP Short Message Gateway (IP-SM-GW) in the IMS converts between SIP and short messages, and connects to Ella SMSC. [Ella IMS](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/sms_over_ip/) includes an IP-SM-GW.

## Store and forward

1. Ella SMSC stores the message, and acknowledges it to the sender.
1. It asks the HSS where the recipient is served: an MME, an SMSF or an IP-SM-GW.
1. It sends the message there.
1. If the phone is unreachable, the HSS records that a message waits, and alerts Ella SMSC when the phone is back. Ella SMSC also retries after the [retry intervals](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/delivery/index.md).

Messages to a phone are delivered one at a time, in order.

A message ends delivered, failed, expired at the end of its validity period, or replaced by a later message. See [Statuses](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/messages/#statuses).

## Messages from applications

Besides phones, applications can send messages to subscribers, for example notifications, one-time codes or updates to SIM cards. Ella SMSC offers them two interfaces:

- The [Messages API](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/messages/index.md): Ella SMSC's HTTP API, for applications you write or script.
- [SMPP](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md): the standard SMSC protocol, for software that already speaks it, such as OTA platforms.

OTA SIM delivery with SMPP

## 3GPP roles

Ella SMSC integrates all three 3GPP functions:

| Function           | Role                                                                                | Diameter procedures (TS 29.338)                                               |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SC, Service Centre | Stores each message until it is delivered or expires.                               |                                                                               |
| SMS-IWMSC          | Receives the messages phones send (mobile originated, MO), and the HSS's alerts.    | MO-Forward-Short-Message, Alert-Service-Centre                                |
| SMS-GMSC           | Finds where a phone is served, and delivers messages to it (mobile terminated, MT). | Send-Routing-Info-for-SM, MT-Forward-Short-Message, Report-SM-Delivery-Status |

# High Availability

A high availability (HA) cluster is several Ella SMSC nodes acting as one service centre, with one service centre address. Every node accepts short messages from phones over Diameter, from ESMEs over SMPP, and from users over the API and UI. Messages, users and settings are shared by every node.

The cluster uses the [Raft](https://raft.github.io/) consensus algorithm. A message is acknowledged to its sender only once a majority of the nodes have stored it, so an acknowledged message survives the loss of any minority of them.

## Failure tolerance

A cluster keeps working as long as a majority of its voting nodes are up.

| Voters | Failures tolerated |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| 1      | 0                  |
| 3      | 1                  |
| 5      | 2                  |

Ella SMSC keeps an odd number of voters, at most 5. Other nodes are standbys, promoted when a voter fails. We recommend 3 or 5 nodes.

## Diameter peers

Each node has its own Diameter host, and they share the realm and the service centre address. Any node receives messages, and the leader delivers them. Connect each Diameter peer to every node, or connect them all through a Diameter routing agent.

## ESMEs

An ESME binds to any node. Its limit of 4 sessions applies across the cluster. Delivery receipts and SIM answers go out through its receiver sessions, on whichever node they are bound.

## Failover

When the leader fails, the other nodes elect a new one within a few seconds. Until then, Ella SMSC answers new messages with a temporary error, so the sender retries, and delivers nothing.

## Draining

Draining a node prepares it for an upgrade or removal: it closes its SMPP sessions, and hands over the leadership. It keeps its Diameter connections and its vote.

## Upgrades

Upgrade one node at a time, one version at a time. The cluster moves to the new version's database once every node runs it. Downgrades are not supported.

## Disaster recovery

If a majority of the voters are lost for good, the cluster stops accepting messages. Restore the last backup on a new cluster. See [Back Up and Restore](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/back_up_and_restore/index.md).

## Further reading

- [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md)
- [Scale a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/scale_ha_cluster/index.md)
- [Perform a Rolling Upgrade](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/rolling_upgrade/index.md)
- [Cluster API](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/cluster/index.md)

# Security

## Users and roles

Everyone who uses the UI or the API is a user with a role: Admin, Read Only, Network Manager or Submitter. The role decides what the user can see and do, from reading settings to managing other users. See [Roles](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/api/#roles).

The first user, an Admin, is created when Ella SMSC is initialized. Admins create the others.

Ella SMSC limits login attempts, from each address and for each account, to slow down password guessing.

## Single sign-on

Users can also log in through the organization's identity provider. See [Single sign-on](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/explanation/single_sign_on/index.md).

## Applications

Applications, such as an OTA platform, use an API token rather than a password. A token belongs to a user and has that user's role, but it cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users. Tokens can expire, and an Admin or the token's user can delete one at any time.

Give each application its own Submitter user: it can send messages, and read only the messages it sent.

## ESMEs

An ESME, such as an OTA platform, binds to the [SMPP listener](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/smpp/index.md) with a `system_id` and a password. SMPP 3.4 limits that password to 8 characters, so Ella SMSC adds other checks:

- Each ESME acts as a user, whose role decides whether it may submit or receive.
- An ESME binds only from the networks in its allow-list. An empty list allows no address.
- Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes. A password the SMSC generates has 8 random letters and digits.
- Binds are limited from each address, and wrong passwords for each ESME. Every refused bind gets the same answer, so a client cannot tell which check failed.
- Only an Admin, logged in rather than with an API token, creates, changes or deletes ESMEs.

SMPP 3.4 has no encryption: the password and the messages cross the network in clear. TLS, with `smpp.tls`, is a common convention outside SMPP 3.4, which the ESME must support. Use plain TCP only over a private link, such as an IPsec VPN, or in a lab.

The allow-list checks the address of the TCP connection. Terminate TLS in Ella SMSC itself, not in a proxy or load balancer, which would hide the ESME's address. On Kubernetes, the Service keeps it with `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`.

## Message content

Messages carry personal content. Reading it is a permission of its own: a Read Only user sees that messages were sent and delivered, but not what they say. Every read of the content is recorded in an [audit event](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/observability/#audit-events), with who read it and from where.

## HTTPS

Ella SMSC serves the UI and the API over plain HTTP unless it is given a certificate in `api.tls` (see the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/reference/config_file/index.md)). Use HTTPS whenever the UI or the API is reachable over a network you do not control.

## Diameter peers

Ella SMSC accepts any Diameter peer that connects and supports S6c or SGd, and its Diameter connections are not encrypted. Keep its Diameter address on a network that only the core network can reach.

Through an edge agent, other networks can send short messages to Ella SMSC, which does not filter them by realm. Have the edge agent accept only the operator's roaming partners.

# Single Sign-On

Users can log in to the UI through the organization's identity provider instead of, or as well as, a password. Ella SMSC works with any OpenID Connect identity provider, such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Ping Identity, Google or Keycloak. To set it up, see [Configure single sign-on](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/configure_single_sign_on/index.md).

Login page with single sign-on

## Password and single sign-on

|                     | Password                                | Single sign-on                                                                    |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Credentials kept by | Ella SMSC                               | The identity provider, with its own policies, such as multi-factor authentication |
| Role set by         | An Admin                                | An Admin, or the user's groups at the identity provider                           |
| Session             | 30 days                                 | The session lifetime, 24 hours by default                                         |
| Access removed by   | Deleting the user in Ella SMSC, at once | Removing the user at the identity provider, at the end of their session           |

Password login stays when single sign-on is on, and at least one Admin always keeps a password. An identity provider that is down or misconfigured cannot lock everyone out.

## Matching users

A user is matched to their account at the identity provider, not to their email address, so a changed or reused email address does not give access to another user. The email address is used once, to link the account at its first login, and only if the identity provider has verified it. A provider that does not say whether email addresses are verified, such as Microsoft Entra ID, must be trusted explicitly: anyone who can set their email address there could take over the matching user. An account with no user in Ella SMSC gets one only from a [group mapping](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/manage_single_sign_on_users/#map-groups-to-roles).

## Offboarding

Ella SMSC does not learn when someone is removed at the identity provider. Their session lasts until its lifetime ends, and their API tokens until deleted. A shorter session lifetime narrows that window, at the cost of logging in more often. To end access at once, [offboard the user](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/manage_single_sign_on_users/#offboard-a-user) in Ella SMSC.

## Client secret

The identity provider's client secret is stored in the database, and so in its [backups](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/how_to/back_up_and_restore/index.md).
